heading: Key Concepts
text: Budgetum is built from a few building blocks. Only categories and transactions are required; everything else is optional. Budget: your plan for a calendar month or a saved custom budget period (for example payday to payday), compared with what actually happened. See Budget screen . Sections: groups of categories, for example Housing, Food, or Income. Categories: what each income or expense belongs to. Every regular income or expense transaction has exactly one category. Sections and categories are one shared list used by every month; plans are separate for each month or period. See Categories and sections . Transactions: income and expense records. They count toward your budget. See Add and edit transactions . Accounts: where money is kept, such as bank, cash, card, savings, or debt. An account can use a currency different from your main (budget) currency. See Accounts . Transfers: moving money between your accounts. A transfer is not spending. Balance adjustments: manual corrections to an account balance. They are not spending either. Contacts: the stores, services, and people you pay or get paid by. See Contacts . Tags: optional labels that cross categories, such as a trip or a project. A transaction can have several tags, and a tag can be on many transactions. See Tags . Receipts: one purchase split into several transactions, each with its own category. Receipts use accounts in your main currency. See Receipts . Recurring transactions and favourites: saved transaction templates. A template can be a favourite, have a repeat schedule, or both. Only active schedules create upcoming transactions, which you confirm. Favourites are added manually: long-press + on Budget or Transactions and pick one. See Recurring transactions . Saved Sets (Pro): saved include/exclude filters for reviewing matching transactions, opening their analytics, or changing them in bulk. Sets can also be shown on the Budget screen with their own plans. See Saved Sets . Bank statement matching (Pro): import a CSV or XLSX bank statement for one account and match its rows to your transactions. In the app it is called Match bank statement . See Bank statement matching . Import / Export: CSV export and import, plus an optional analytics ZIP for Desktop Analytics. See Settings . Desktop Analytics: private reports on a computer at budgetum.app/analytics. Your export is read in the browser, not uploaded. Free and Pro: core budgeting is free. Free allows up to 5 tags and 5 recurring templates . Budgetum Pro is a one-time purchase that removes those limits and unlocks Saved Sets and bank statement matching.

heading: Rules That Apply Everywhere
text: Budgetum is flexible and does not force a budgeting method. See Budgetum philosophy . Transfers and balance adjustments change account balances only. They never count as budget income or spending, and Analytics leaves them out. Analytics uses saved transactions in the selected date range; upcoming recurring previews are not included. Changing the dates keeps your whole drill-down selection. Refunds: the Analytics summary shows gross expenses and income, with refunds counted in received income. Expense breakdowns show net amounts after refunds. For example, a $100 purchase and a $20 refund in the same category show as $80 in the breakdown. Tags in Analytics: a transaction with several tags is divided equally between them, refunds included. A $100 expense tagged A and B counts $50 toward each tag, so a tag's amount in a breakdown can differ from the total of its full transaction list. See Analytics and reports . Foreign-currency accounts: budget totals use the transaction's budget amount in your main currency, while the account balance uses the amount in the account's own currency. Scheduled recurring transactions can require confirmation. While any are waiting, the Transactions tab shows a small ? badge. Make a backup before importing a CSV. Re-importing a Budgetum export skips transactions that already exist (matched by their ID). Contact and tag fields on the Add Transaction form can be hidden with Show on transaction creation in the Contacts and Tags screen settings.

The Budget Screen is the main screen of Budgetum where you can view and manage your budget for either a calendar month or a custom budget period. It shows how much you planned to spend or earn, how much you’ve actually spent or received so far, and how you’re tracking toward your goals.

heading: Accessing the Budget Screen
text: The Budget Screen is the app’s home screen. You can access it by: Opening the app (it opens by default) Tapping the Budget tab in the bottom navigation

heading: Rating invitation
text: After either 7 elapsed days since the recorded first-open date or at least 10 saved transactions across the app, an Enjoying Budgetum? card can appear below the summary and before the remaining budget content. If the summary is hidden, the card is at the top of the scrollable content. It is available to free and Pro users; previous rating-invitation dismissals or rating actions can prevent it from appearing. × / Close , at the top right of the card, permanently hides it on Budget and clears the rating-related dot on More . The More rating card remains available without a close button. Restarting the app or changing periods does not bring the Budget card back. Rate App opens the App Store review form on iOS or the Google Play listing on Android, where you select the stars under Rate this app . Successfully opening the store hides both invitation cards, even if you return without submitting a rating. If the store cannot open, an error appears and the cards remain available. The regular Rate App row in More remains available afterward. A separate feedback invitation may still cause a More dot. See More — Rate App for eligibility details and the separate feedback invitation.

heading: Add Transaction and favourite shortcut
text: Long-press the + button at the bottom center to open Favourites . This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on Recurring Transactions ; those controls are not shown in this shortcut.

heading: Period selector (top bar)
text: At the top of the screen you’ll see the currently selected budget period. This can be: A calendar month: Current month for the actual current month; otherwise, just the month name if it is in the current year (for example, September when the current year is 2026), or the month and year for another year (for example, September 2025 ) A custom budget period with its own name A custom budget period shown by date range when no name was given Actions: Tap the period name to open the full period picker In the picker, switch between Month and Other Periods The Month tab shows available months with income and expense totals The Other Periods tab shows your saved custom budget periods grouped into Future, Active, and Previous In the Other Periods tab, tap Add in the header to create a new custom budget period An Edit button with a calendar icon (tooltip Edit ) always appears next to the period name. It opens the editor for whatever is currently selected: the calendar month, or the custom period. When a past or future calendar month is selected, a Back to current month button with a curved back arrow appears without a filled background above the Summary Card and stays visible while the budget content scrolls. Tap it to select the current calendar month and show its budget immediately, without opening the period picker or a confirmation. The button then disappears. If the Summary Card is hidden in Display Settings, the button still appears at the top of the budget content. It is not shown for the current month or for any custom budget period. Returning does not change existing transactions or plans.

heading: Editing the selected month
text: When a calendar month is selected, tap Edit next to the period name. The screen title is that month (for example, September 2026 ). Budget amount (optional) Tap the field to open the Number Picker (titled Budget amount ) Helper text: Leave empty to use planned income. Clear a saved amount with the × on the field Entering 0 is treated as empty If you set an amount greater than 0, the Summary Card’s first column is labeled Budget instead of Income , and that amount is used as the period’s main income/budget total instead of planned income from income categories Income section Switch labeled Income section Helper: Show or hide the income section on the budget screen. On (the default): income categories and income totals appear as usual Off: the income section is hidden on Budget for that month Tap the checkmark in the top bar to save. Leaving without saving (Back or close) discards the changes. These month settings apply only to that calendar month and are separate from a custom period’s settings. When a custom period is selected: The same Edit button opens the custom period editor (see Custom Budget Periods ) A small history icon appears in the title if the period is already in the past The Budget screen uses that period's exact date range instead of a calendar month

heading: Top-right actions
text: The Budget screen has three main actions in the top-right corner: Analytics (pie chart) — opens Analytics & Reports for the currently selected budget period Settings — opens Display Settings directly so you can quickly change how the Budget screen looks and what totals mean Menu (☰) — opens additional actions The menu icon (☰) opens: New Expense Section — create a new budget section to group categories Add Category — add a new income or expense category Change Order — rearrange sections and categories Display Settings — another way to open the same display/settings screen Copy Plan — import selected category plans from another month or custom period into the current one Export PDF — configure export settings, create a PDF snapshot, or generate a link to a web copy of the current budget plan Collapse Sections — collapse all sections at once for a more compact view

heading: Summary Card
text: At the top of the budget screen there’s a Summary Card showing your overall financial picture for the currently selected period.

heading: Three-column view
text: When you have both income and expenses: Income — planned income (gray) and actual income received (income color). If the selected month or custom period has a Budget amount set, this column is labeled Budget instead of Income Expenses — planned expenses (gray) and actual spending (primary color) Remaining — the difference between income and expenses

heading: Visual indicators
text: Progress bars between columns fill from bottom to top against the summary’s planned amounts. Above the expense plan, the full bar represents total spending: the primary-colored lower portion is covered by the plan and the red upper portion is the excess, separated by a thin divider. A plan of 500 with 1,000 spent produces equal portions. Small excesses keep their exact proportions, without a minimum red size or extra text. The same expense split appears in the horizontal bar when only expenses are shown and in the expanded Needs and Wants bars. Income and Savings progress use the income color for the planned share and a lighter green for amounts above a positive plan, with a thin divider between them. Progress requires planned values to be enabled and a positive actual amount. A zero or missing plan does not hide progress: expenses show fully red, while income and Savings show fully in the income color, without a divider. This applies to vertical summary bars, single-line bars, and the expanded type bars. Zero or negative actual amounts have no progress fill. These indicators use the summary’s planned totals, including adjustments from Include category overspending in summary totals , so they can differ from individual section or category indicators. Colored amounts indicate status: Income color — income or a positive balance Primary color — expenses within budget Red — overspending or a negative balance Difference shows how much you’re over or under your plan

heading: Expense breakdown (tap to expand)
text: If your expenses are grouped by type (Needs, Wants, Savings), tap the Summary Card to expand and see: Needs (🔒) — essential expenses like rent, utilities, groceries Wants (❤️) — non-essential spending like entertainment, dining out, fun purchases Savings (🐷) — money set aside for savings and investments Each type shows: Percentage of total expenses Planned vs actual amounts Progress bar toward the plan Filter by type: Tap Needs , Wants , or Savings to filter the entire budget view and show only categories of that type.

heading: Visual circles mode (optional)
text: If Circle Shortcuts is enabled under Display Settings → Circles , a grid of circular progress indicators appears near the top of the Budget screen (up to five section circles per row). You can tap anywhere in a circle's surrounding tile to open it: The Income circle appears only when the section has at least one category available in the selected budget. It remains visible even when the selected month or budget period has no income plans or transactions, unless income is hidden in that budget’s settings. Show all sections overrides that hiding for circle shortcuts. Selecting a Needs / Wants / Savings filter hides income circles. Each circle shows the section icon and fills based on spending progress A fully filled circle means you’ve reached the budget limit A red segment in an expense circle indicates the portion of spending above its plan With progress shown, section and category circles use the same proportional split as the section and category bars described below, without reducing border opacity for missing plans. Expense activity above a zero or missing plan displays a full red ring. With progress hidden for sections or categories, circles with a non-zero actual amount show a complete, solid border in their section color, regardless of the plan or overspending. Circles with a zero actual amount use the same muted neutral border as the unfilled track when progress is shown. Icons and category names keep their usual appearance. To show unused sections too, open the Budget screen’s top-right Settings (gear) → Circles and turn on Show all sections . This is off by default and is disabled while Circle Shortcuts is off. Your choice is saved, including when you switch circles off and back on. Return to Budget to see the change. With Show all sections off, expense shortcuts require at least one category with a plan or transactions in the selected period. The Income exception above still applies. With it on, all sections with categories are available, including sections outside the selected custom budget and income sections hidden from the budget list. Sections without selectable categories are omitted. This affects circle shortcuts; it does not add plans or change the section list or budget totals. Circle amounts and progress use the selected month or custom date range. With Show all sections on, they include activity in categories excluded from a restricted custom budget. The main budget totals and section list still follow that budget’s restrictions, so circle amounts can differ from the budget list. Adding a transaction through an excluded category’s circle does not link that category to the custom budget; it can remain excluded from its totals. Needs / Wants / Savings still filters the shortcuts. With Show all sections on, matching categories without plans or transactions remain available. When Show all sections is on and a section has no categories with plans or transactions matching the active filter, tapping it shows its available categories immediately. Otherwise, unused categories remain behind the reveal control described below. Tapping a section circle opens a bottom sheet for that section. The sheet shows: A short section summary (name, icon, and the same kinds of spent / planned / remaining / progress details controlled by your section display settings) A grid of category circles for that section (filtered by Needs / Wants / Savings when that filter is active on the Budget screen). Category names use up to three lines; longer names end with an ellipsis. Long-press a category circle and choose Edit to read its full name. Optional actual amount text under a category circle when your display settings show transaction amounts and the category has a non-zero actual If the section has hidden categories, a Show more (+N) control reveals them in the same grid Tapping a category circle or its surrounding tile closes the sheet and opens the Add Transaction screen for that category (single-entry / save-and-close mode). Long-press a section circle to open the same options as the section header's long-press or ⋮ menu (see Section actions ). Long-press a category circle , including its surrounding tile, to close the category picker and open the same options as the category row. The same action availability rules apply as in the list. These shortcuts also work when Options Button is off. To plan an existing unused category, tap its section circle, then Show more (+N) if the category is hidden. Long-press the category circle → Edit → Planned Amount , enter a non-negative amount, then tap the top-right checkmark to save. Saving creates a plan for the selected month or custom budget if the category did not have one. The active Needs / Wants / Savings filter still limits which categories appear; clear or change it on the Budget screen if needed. After editing or dismissing the category options, you return to Budget; tap the section again to reopen its category picker. The unused-category reveal is reset when the picker reopens, unless Show all sections automatically reveals those categories because the section has no visible planned or active categories. There is no longer an Add (plus) circle in circles mode. To add a category, use the section menu in the list below, or More → Advanced Features → Categories .

heading: Sets on Budget (Pro)
text: Turn on Display Settings → Sets → Show Sets to show a collapsible Sets block below the Summary Card and circle shortcuts, above the budget sections. Show Sets is off by default. Sets has its own switches for actual amounts, planned amounts, remaining amounts, percentages, and progress, independent of the category settings. Only actual amounts are on by default; the other set-item switches are off. Hiding the block or an amount preserves watched sets and saved plans. Sets requires Pro; the switches are disabled without Pro, and the block is hidden. The item switches are disabled while Show Sets is off.

heading: Add and arrange watched sets
text: Expand the Sets block and tap Add Set . If Action Buttons is off, long-press the block title or use its ⋮ → Add Set instead. Tap the Set field to open Select Set , or tap a quick-select chip below the field. Chips scroll horizontally and select a set without saving the form. The selection page lists sets not already on Budget. Its search icon shows a search field; searching matches set names, and hiding search clears it. Its + icon opens Create Set; after saving, the new set is selected automatically and you return to the plan form, like other selection pages. The list uses a bordered card with initial-letter circles, like the tag picker. Condition icons beneath each name match the Sets index, including red outlines for excluded conditions. A checkmark identifies the selected set. Back without selecting preserves the form’s selection. If no sets are available, use + to create one. The next row contains Planned amount , initially empty. Plan type always appears after the amount, including for sets based on tags or other conditions. It defaults to Expense ; choose Income for a positive net target. Editing an existing plan preserves its saved plan type. Fields stack on narrow screens or with larger text. Enter the magnitude as a non-negative number. The plan applies to the budget period from which you opened the form. The amount helper says: “Leave empty to track without a plan.” Tap the top-right checkmark to save. Back without saving discards changes to this form; a set already created from the selection page remains saved. Watched sets are global: once added, a set appears in all calendar months and custom periods. You do not add it again each period. On the Sets screen, a link icon beside the set name means it is included here. That set’s menu offers Add to Budget or Unlink from Budget , which adds or removes it immediately without opening this plan form. Add to Budget requires Pro. See Watching sets on Budget . Change Order in the block's menu opens the existing Sets ordering screen; that order applies both here and on Sets. When opened from Budget, it shows all saved sets, with sets not watched on Budget dimmed to indicate that they are not visible in the block. Dimmed sets remain reorderable; dragging them does not add them to Budget. From the main Sets screen, all entries have normal opacity. Tap the block header to collapse or expand it. The eye icon on the right side of the header shows or hides sets without transactions for this period. A count just after that icon, on the right side of the header, shows how many sets are currently displayed. The same action is in the block menu. Long-press menus remain available when Options Button hides ⋮ controls. An empty block explains how to add sets. Loading shows a progress indicator; a load failure offers a retry instead of showing zero totals.

heading: Amounts and matching transactions
text: With the default set-item switches, each row shows the set’s name and actual net amount. Income minus expenses determines the net, with refunds included in that calculation. Like category spending amounts, net spending is displayed without a minus sign; net income has a + prefix and uses the income section color, whether the plan is empty, zero, or positive. A set with no matching transactions remains visible with 0 unless you hide empty sets. The eye icon on the Sets header and Hide sets without transactions in the block menu hide watched sets with no matching transactions in the selected period, including recurring previews when future transactions are included. Hiding empty sets does not unlink them. If every watched set is hidden, the block explains that none have transactions in this period. Change Order still lists all saved sets. Currency formatting and Hide numbers apply as elsewhere in Budget. The block uses the selected budget period's dates , replacing each set's saved dates for this view without editing the set. All other set conditions still apply. The block does not restrict sets to a custom budget's selected categories and does not apply the Needs / Wants / Savings filter. Its amounts can therefore cover transactions outside the main budget sections. Set amounts and plans never add to Budget's main summary totals. Include future transactions in budget controls saved future/planned transactions and matching recurring previews in the Budget block's amounts. When off, both are excluded from those amounts. Tap a set row, or choose Transactions in its menu, to open the set's transactions for the same period. The transaction screen uses its usual History and Upcoming views, including matching future transactions and recurring previews regardless of this Budget setting. Returning keeps the Budget period and watched sets. Analytics opens the set's analytics for the selected dates, using that screen's usual controls. The Sets block has no combined total. Its rows are independent views of their matching transactions. The Sets block is not included in budget PDF exports or web-share snapshots.

heading: Set plans
text: Plan amounts are separate for every month or custom period, with no automatic carryover. An empty Planned amount means there is no plan for that period. Remaining, percentage, progress, and the planned value are hidden; the actual net appears beside the name when any amount or progress switch is enabled. New plans start empty. Entering 0 saves a real zero plan and enables plan comparisons according to the display switches. × / Clear plan empties the field, including when it contains 0; save to remove the plan for this period without unlinking the set. Edit Set Plan in a row's ⋮ or long-press menu opens the same Planned amount / Plan type form with the set fixed. The amount changes only the displayed period. The plan type is global for that watched set and controls plan comparisons across periods; it does not change the set's conditions or displayed net. Expense compares the plan against expenses minus income and refunds. A plan of 500, expenses of 400, and income of 100 means 300 net spending and 200 left. Income compares the plan against income minus expenses. A plan of 500, income of 700, and expenses of 300 means 400 net income and 100 left to reach the target. Tap Planned amount to open the Number Picker. Negative amounts are not allowed. Clear the field with × to remove the plan, or confirm 0 in the picker to save a zero plan. Save with the top-right checkmark; Back discards unsaved changes. Display Settings → Sets has the same item controls as categories, but changing them affects only set rows: Total Transaction Amount , Planned Amount , Remaining/Overspent , Percentage of Remaining/Overspent , and Progress Indicator . Rows use the category layout: remaining or over-plan amounts beside the name, actual / planned amounts below, the remaining percentage on the right, and a progress bar underneath when enabled. Percentage is remaining divided by plan (for example, 50 spent against 100 planned leaves 50%). Above a positive plan it shows the excess percentage in the same color as category over-plan values. At exactly the plan, the remaining amount and percentage are hidden. With a saved 0 plan, the planned amount shows 0 when enabled. Positive activity in the plan’s direction is entirely over plan: the percentage shows 100%, and progress is fully filled (red for Expense plans, income color for Income plans). With no activity, remaining and percentage are hidden and progress has no fill. Activity opposite to the plan’s direction shows 0% and no progress fill. Only an empty plan hides all plan comparisons and disables over-plan coloring. These switches work independently, so Percentage of Remaining/Overspent can be shown while Planned Amount is hidden. When the planned value is visible and Quick plan update is on, tap its dotted underline in the Budget row to update this period's amount directly. With Quick plan update off, use Edit Set Plan . The quick picker may offer the current positive net amount in the plan's direction as a shortcut. Copy Plan includes eligible watched sets alongside categories. Choose the source period, select the sets to copy, and save. Only sets with a saved source plan and an empty destination plan appear. A saved 0 plan can be copied and prevents an existing destination plan from being overwritten. Clear the destination plan first if you want to copy another plan into that period. Copying changes neither the global watched list nor plan types. Set plans can be copied even while their Budget display is hidden. Deleted custom periods are not available as Copy Plan sources. Edit Set opens the full filter editor and preserves the Budget selection and plans. Unlink from Budget uses a broken-link icon and immediately removes the set from this block in every period, without deleting the saved set or its period plans. Adding it again restores any plan saved for the selected period. Deleting the saved set itself on Sets removes it and its plans.

heading: Budget sections
text: Your budget is organized into sections (for example, “Housing”, “Transportation”, “Income”, etc.). Each section contains related categories.

heading: Section header
text: Each section shows: Section icon and name — its identity with a custom color Arrow indicator — whether the section is expanded (↑) or collapsed (↓) Amount left or Amount spent — depending on your display settings Progress bar (optional) — visual indicator of spending vs plan Percentage (optional) — how much of the budget is used or remaining

heading: Expand/collapse sections
text: Tap anywhere on the section header to expand or collapse it Expanded sections show all categories inside The app remembers which sections you expanded

heading: Section actions (long press or menu)
text: Long-press a section header (or tap the ⋮ menu if it’s shown) to access: New Income Source or New Expense Category — add a new category to this section (label depends on section type) Transactions — view all transactions in this section Trends — view a plan vs actual chart by month Analytics — open charts and reports for this section Edit — change the section name, icon, or color Delete Plan — remove the budget plan (only if there are no transactions) Delete — permanently remove the section (only if it has no categories)

heading: Budget categories
text: Inside each section you’ll see categories (for example, “Groceries”, “Electricity”, “Salary”, etc.).

heading: Category display
text: Each category shows: Category name — with a recurring icon (↻) if it’s linked to recurring transactions Amount left or Amount spent — depending on your display settings Spent / Planned — actual spending versus the budgeted amount Tappable planned amount — when planned amounts are visible and Quick plan update is on, the planned value is shown with a subtle dotted underline to indicate that you can tap it. When Quick plan update is off, the amount is not underlined and is not tappable Percentage — how much of the category budget is used or remaining Progress bar (optional) — visual indicator of spending progress

heading: Color coding
text: Section color — normal spending within budget Red — overspending (exceeded the planned amount) Gray — remaining amount to spend Section and category progress bars, circle rings, and the section summary bar inside the circle category picker show exact proportions: Up to the plan, the section-colored fill shows actual spending relative to the plan; the rest is an empty gray track. A plan of 500 with 250 spent fills half the indicator. Above an expense plan, the full indicator represents total spending. The section-colored portion is the amount covered by the plan; the red portion is the excess. A plan of 500 with 1,000 spent is half section color and half red; with 600 spent, one-sixth is red. A thin divider marks where the section-colored portion meets the red excess in bars and rings. It appears only when both portions are present; it does not enlarge the red portion. Red segments have no minimum size. Spending 501 against a 500 plan produces a very small red segment that may be hard to see. Existing amount colors still apply; no additional overspending label is added. Positive expense spending with a zero or missing plan is fully red. Zero or negative net spending (for example, after refunds) leaves the indicator empty. Income uses its section color up to the plan. Above a positive income plan, bars and rings show the planned share in the section color and the surplus in a lighter green, separated by a thin divider. With 500 planned and 1,000 received, each portion occupies half the indicator. Positive income with a zero or missing plan keeps a full section-colored indicator. No divider appears at or below the plan, or with a zero or missing plan. These rules apply when the corresponding section or category progress display is enabled. The summary card’s indicators and their display conditions are described under Summary Card above.

heading: Category actions
text: Tap a category to view all transactions for that category. Tap the planned amount in the category row to quickly change that category’s planned value without opening the full edit screen. This is available only when Quick plan update is on in Display Settings (it is on by default). It opens the Number Picker with the current planned amount prefilled. If the category has actual spending, the picker can also offer that spent amount as a one-tap quick-select value. When Quick plan update is off, use Edit on the category instead. Long-press a category (or tap the ⋮ menu if shown) to access: Add Transaction — quickly add a new transaction to this category Transactions — view all transactions for this category Trends — view a plan vs actual chart by month Analytics — open charts and detailed reports Edit — change the category name, planned amount, or settings Delete Plan — remove the budget plan for this month (only if there are no transactions) Delete — permanently remove the category (only if there are no transactions and no recurring templates)

heading: Adding categories to a section
text: At the bottom of each expanded section there’s a New Income Source or New Expense Category button to quickly create a new category within that section. These in-list buttons appear only when Action Buttons is on in Display Settings (it is on by default). The ☰ menu still offers Add Category when the buttons are hidden.

heading: Edit Section screen
text: Opened when you choose Edit from a section’s long-press or ⋮ menu. Use it to change the section’s identity and appearance. Fields and actions: Section name — text field; required. Duplicate names (compared to other sections) are not allowed. Icon — tap to open an icon picker (bottom sheet). Different icon sets for income vs expense sections. Color — tap to open a color picker: “Default” (app primary) or a grid of preset colors. Saving: Tap the ✓ (check) button in the app bar. Validation runs before save (non-empty name, no duplicate).

heading: Edit Category screen
text: Opened when you choose Edit from a category’s long-press or ⋮ menu. Use it to change the category’s name, section, type, and (when editing from the budget) its planned amount. Fields and actions: Section — read-only for income categories; for expense categories, tap to open a section picker and move the category to another expense section. Category name — text field; required. Duplicate names (compared to other categories) are not allowed. Category type (expense categories only) — Needs , Wants , or Savings with short descriptions. Used for the Summary Card breakdown and filtering. Planned amount (when not hidden) — tap to open a number picker. Required and must be ≥ 0. An icon opens History for this category (spending history screen). Last months’ history — when the category has plan/actual data, a block shows the last several months with planned vs actual amounts and a progress bar. Tap an actual or planned amount to copy it into the planned amount field for the current month. Saving: Tap the ✓ (check) button in the app bar. Validation: non-empty name, no duplicate name, valid amount (when amount is shown). When opened from the budget screen, both the category and its plan are updated; when opened from elsewhere (e.g. categories screen) with plan hidden, only the category (name, section, type) is updated.

heading: Copy a budget plan from another period
text: If you’re starting a new month or custom period and want to use an existing plan as a template: Tap the menu button (☰) in the top right Select Copy Plan Choose the month or custom period you want to copy from Review the list of category plans from that source period Select the categories you want to import, then tap the check button to apply them Important details: Budgetum imports only the selected category plans , not a forced full clone of the entire source budget Categories that already exist in the current target period are skipped and do not appear in the import list When a previous plan source is found automatically, Budgetum preselects all eligible categories so you can import them faster A Copy Plan button also appears below the sections when Action Buttons is on, the current selection has at most one category with a plan, and other plan sources are available. The ☰ menu still offers Copy Plan when the in-list button is hidden. New month reminder When a new calendar month starts, the Budget screen can ask A new month has started . The dialog shows last month (for example, From last month: November 2026 ) and offers Copy Plan and Not now . Copy Plan switches Budget to the current month if last month was still selected, then opens the same Copy Plan screen with last month already chosen as the source and all its categories preselected; review them, untick any you don't need, and tap the check button to copy. Not now (or tapping outside) closes the dialog; you can still use Copy Plan from the ☰ menu at any time. The reminder appears at most once per month, when you open the app or return to it from the background while the Budget tab is shown and no other screen is open. If you are on another tab at that moment, it waits until the next time. It appears only if: the current month or last month is selected (not an older or later month, and not a custom period). Budget reopens on the month you viewed last, so on the first open of a new month it usually still shows last month last month has plans (category plans, or set plans with Pro) this month has no plans yet (no category plans, and no set plans with Pro); once you plan anything in the new month, the reminder is not shown If last month had no plans, Budgetum does not ask, even when an older month or a custom period has plans. Ended custom periods have their own dialog; see Custom Budget Periods .

heading: Export budget as PDF or web link
text: Use Export PDF from the Budget screen menu to open the budget export flow for the period you are currently viewing. Export settings (gear icon on the export screen): Group by expense type — group expense categories under Needs, Wants, and Savings when applicable Show section titles — include section headings in the output Show planned values / Show actual values — at least one must stay on; both can be included in PDF and web share PDF preview: Live preview of the report; use the system share/print actions from the preview bar to save or send the PDF Web share link (link icon on the preview bar): Generates a read-only web view of the budget plan for the selected period Choose whether the shared view includes planned and/or actual amounts (at least one required) Copy the URL to share; links expire after a limited number of days (shown when the link is ready) Other details: The export follows the active period selector (month or custom budget period) Change the selected period on the Budget screen before exporting if you need a different range Shared links expose budget structure and amounts you include—share only with people you trust

heading: “New Expense Section” button
text: Below your existing sections (and the Copy Plan button when it’s shown) there’s a New Expense Section button to create a new budget grouping. It appears only when Action Buttons is on. The ☰ menu still offers New Expense Section when the button is hidden.

heading: Getting started help
text: When you first start using the app, a helpful guide appears at the bottom of the Budget Screen with tips on: Making a list of expected expenses for the month Grouping them into sections Adding transactions to track actual expenses It also shows section examples (e.g. Housing, Travel, Car). You can dismiss this guide once you’re comfortable.

heading: Display customization
text: You can customize the Budget Screen to show exactly what you need. Open Display Settings from the top-right Settings button or from the menu.

heading: General options
text: Quick plan update — tap a category’s planned amount to update it directly. On by default. When off, the planned amount is not tappable or underlined. Options Button — show or hide the ⋮ menu buttons on sections and categories. When off, options appear on long press instead of a button. Action Buttons — show buttons for adding sections and categories or copying a plan. On by default. When off, the in-list Copy Plan , New Expense Section , and New Income Source / New Expense Category buttons are hidden; the ☰ menu still has those actions. Include Upcoming Transactions in Budget — include or exclude future-dated transactions from the current budget totals. When this is on, upcoming transactions already affect the Budget screen's actual totals and progress bars. When it is off, the Budget screen only counts transactions that are not in the future.

heading: Circles options
text: Circle Shortcuts — show or hide the section circle grid; on by default. Show all sections — include all sections with categories, regardless of the selected budget; off by default. Available only while Circle Shortcuts is on. See Visual circles mode for display rules and tapping behavior.

heading: Summary card options
text: Hide summary card — hide the Summary Card on the Budget screen. Off by default. When it is on, the card is gone; the Back to current month button still appears when a past or future calendar month is selected. Show/hide planned values Show/hide actual values Show/hide the difference column/value Hide Decimals — show Summary Card amounts rounded to whole numbers (for example 1,235 instead of 1,234.56 ). On by default. Turn it off to see exact amounts with cents in the Income, Expenses, and remaining values. The Needs / Wants / Savings amounts on the card follow the same setting. Applies to the Budget screen only. Only display changes; totals are calculated from the exact amounts either way. Include category overspending in summary totals. When this is on, any amount spent above a category's plan is added to the summary card's planned totals, so the overall remaining amount reflects that overspending more realistically. If either planned values or actual values are hidden, the Difference setting becomes unavailable because the comparison needs both values.

heading: Section display options
text: Show/hide planned amounts Show/hide spent amounts Show/hide remaining amounts Show/hide remaining percentage Show/hide progress bars

heading: Category display options
text: Show/hide planned amounts Show/hide spent amounts Show/hide remaining amounts Show/hide remaining percentage Show/hide progress bars

heading: Tips for using the Budget Screen
text: Check it regularly — open the Budget Screen daily or weekly Use sections wisely — group related expenses for easier management Watch the colors — red means overspending Tap for details — tap any category to see exactly where your money went Filter by type — focus on Needs, Wants, or Savings Copy previous budgets — use Copy Plan to save time

Custom Budget Periods let you budget across any date range instead of being limited to a calendar month. You can create named or unnamed periods, switch the Budget screen into that period, and keep separate plans for those custom ranges. This feature is managed from the Budget screen's period picker.

heading: Accessing Custom Budget Periods
text: You can access custom budget periods by: Opening the Budget screen Tapping the current period in the top bar Switching from Month to Other Periods An Edit button with a calendar icon (tooltip Edit ) always appears next to the period name in the Budget screen header. When a custom period is selected, it opens that period’s editor. When a calendar month is selected, it opens the month editor instead (see Budget Screen ).

heading: What a Custom Budget Period Changes
text: When you select a custom period: The Budget screen uses that period's start and end dates instead of a calendar month Budget plans are loaded from that custom period instead of monthly plans Transactions and recurring previews are limited to that selected date range The top bar shows the custom period name, or its date range if it has no name If the selected period ends before today, the Budget screen header also shows a small history icon to make it clear that you are viewing a past period.

heading: Period Picker Layout
text: The Budget period picker opens as a full-screen selector with two tabs in the title area: Month - Standard month-based budgeting Other Periods - Your custom budget periods

heading: Month Tab
text: The Month tab works like the normal month selector: Choose any month See income and expense totals on the tiles Switch the global budget view back to monthly mode Selecting a month automatically clears the active custom budget period and returns the app to month-based budgeting.

heading: Other Periods Tab
text: The Other Periods tab shows your saved custom periods grouped by timing: Future - Periods that have not started yet Active - Periods that include today Previous - Periods that already ended Future and Previous groups can be collapsed or expanded. The Active group stays open. Previous periods load their totals when the group is expanded. If there are no saved custom periods yet, the screen shows an empty state with a button to create one.

heading: Period Card Information
text: Each custom period card can show: Name - Optional custom title Date range - The start and end dates Planned badges - Planned income and planned expenses Actual badges - Actual income and actual expenses in the period Trailing total - The current remainder/balance for the period Selection highlight - Indicates the active budget period More button - Opens actions for that period If a period has a custom name, the picker shows that name with the date range underneath. If there is no custom name, the date range is used as the main title.

heading: Selecting a Custom Period
text: Tap a period card to switch the Budget screen to that period. When the picker is being used for full budget switching: The selected custom period becomes the active budget scope The Budget screen reloads immediately The picker closes after the new period is applied The Use this period action in the more menu does the same thing.

heading: Creating or Editing a Custom Period
text: Use the Add button in the picker header, or open an existing period and choose Edit . The editor contains these fields:

heading: Name
text: Optional Lets you give the period a short label like Paycheck Cycle , Vacation , or School Term If left empty, Budgetum displays the date range instead

heading: Start Date and End Date
text: Define the exact inclusive range of the period If you move one boundary past the other, the editor automatically keeps the dates in a valid order

heading: Budget Amount
text: Optional If left empty, planned income is based on the period's income-category plans If set, the custom amount becomes the period's main income/budget total on the Budget screen

heading: All Transactions
text: This switch controls whether the Budget screen includes only planned categories or the full category set inside the date range. On - Show all transactions in the selected date range, including categories that do not have a plan in this custom period Off - Limit the budget view to categories linked to this custom period's plans (while still allowing related planned sections to appear)

heading: Income Section
text: This switch controls whether the income section is visible while that custom period is active. On - Show income categories and income totals normally Off - Hide the income section from the Budget screen for this period

heading: Saving
text: Tap the checkmark in the top bar to save the period. When you create a new period from the picker, Budgetum saves it, reloads the list, and automatically switches the Budget screen to the newly created period.

heading: Managing Existing Periods
text: Open the more menu on a period card, or long-press the card, to access: Use this period - Apply it to the Budget screen Edit - Change its name, dates, or options Delete - Remove the custom period after confirmation Deleting a custom period also deletes the plans stored specifically for that period. If you delete the period that is currently selected, Budgetum returns the budget view to normal month mode.

heading: When a Period Ends
text: If the custom period selected on the Budget screen has ended, Budgetum asks once what to do next. The dialog appears the next time you open the app or return to it from the background while the Budget tab is shown and no other screen is open. If you are on another tab at that moment, it waits until the next time. It is titled "<period> has ended" , using the period's name or its date range, and shows the next dates. Not now — closes the dialog. The period stays selected and the dialog does not appear again for it. Tapping outside the dialog does the same. Move dates — keeps the same period and changes its dates to the next ones. Its plans and settings stay as they are. The period's previous results are no longer shown as a separate period; your transactions are not changed. When the new dates end, Budgetum asks again. Create next period — creates a new period with the next dates and selects it. The new period gets the same Budget amount, All Transactions and Income Section settings, and a copy of all category plans and set plans. The ended period stays unchanged in the Previous group. Next dates: A period covering whole months continues by the same number of months, following the calendar. For example, Sep 1 – Sep 30 continues as Oct 1 – Oct 31, Sep 15 – Oct 14 as Oct 15 – Nov 14, and Jan 1 – Dec 31 as the next full year. Any other period continues with the same number of days. For example, a 14-day period Sep 6 – Sep 19 continues as Sep 20 – Oct 3. If several cycles were missed while the app was not opened, Budgetum goes straight to the cycle that includes today. It does not create the periods in between. Name: if the name ends with its only number, the number goes up by one per cycle: Paycheck 3 becomes Paycheck 4 , and Budget 2026 becomes Budget 2027 . Other names are kept as they are, including names with a date range or more than one number. Two periods can have the same name; the picker shows each one's dates. When the dialog does not appear: The period has no plans: no category or section plans, no set plans, and no Budget amount. A period with exactly the next dates already exists. You chose an already-ended period in the picker, for example to review past spending from Previous . You saved the period in the editor with an end date in the past. The dialog was already shown for this period, even if the app was closed without answering it. The selected period has not ended yet, or a calendar month is selected.

heading: Using Plans with Custom Periods
text: Custom periods keep their own budget plans, separate from monthly plans. This means: A category can have one plan for March 2026 and a different plan for a custom period that overlaps March Copy/import plan actions can use monthly plans or another custom period as the source Reopening the same custom period restores its saved plan values This also makes custom periods useful as plan templates . For example, you can keep reusable periods for things like pay cycles, travel budgets, seasonal spending, or event planning, then copy those plans into a new month or another custom period when needed.

heading: Tips for Using Custom Budget Periods
text: Name repeated periods clearly - Labels like Paycheck 1 , Paycheck 2 , or Summer Trip make them easier to recognize in the picker. Use a custom budget amount for fixed-cycle budgeting - This is helpful when you budget against a paycheck amount rather than planned income categories. Turn off All Transactions for stricter budgeting - This keeps the view focused on categories that are actually part of the custom plan. Hide income when it is not useful - For spending-only periods, turning off the income section can simplify the screen. Review past periods from the Previous group - It is useful for checking completed trips, pay cycles, or short-term plans without changing your monthly history.

The Transactions Screen shows budget transactions for the budget period you select - that is, income and expense transactions that are linked to your budget categories. This includes transactions from all accounts but excludes pure transfers between accounts and balance adjustments (unless they're combined with a categorized transaction). Transactions are organized by date so you can review your financial activity and track spending for the chosen period.

heading: Accessing the Transactions Screen
text: You can access the Transactions Screen by: Tapping the "Transactions" tab in the bottom navigation If there are scheduled transactions that still require confirmation, the Transactions tab shows a small question-mark badge as a reminder.

heading: Period Selector (Top Bar)
text: At the top of the screen, the selected budget period is displayed. This can be: A calendar month: Current month for the actual current month; otherwise, just the month name if it is in the current year (for example, September when the current year is 2026), or the month and year for another year (for example, September 2025 ) A custom budget period with its own name A custom budget period shown by date range when it has no name All data on the screen - summary and transaction list - follows that selected budget period. Actions: Tap the period name to open the budget period picker Switch between Month and Other Periods Choose another month or a saved custom budget period When a past or future calendar month is selected, a Back to current month button with a curved back arrow appears without a filled background above the Summary Card. It stays visible while the transaction list scrolls. Tap it to return to the current calendar month without opening the period picker or a confirmation; the summary and list update, and the button disappears. The selected History or Upcoming view is preserved. The button is hidden for the current month and for all custom budget periods. Returning does not change existing transactions or plans.

heading: Top Bar Buttons
text: The top bar contains several action buttons: Calendar Icon - Opens the Daily Transactions view where you can browse transactions by specific dates on a calendar Repeat Icon - Opens the Recurring Transactions screen to manage subscriptions, bills, and regular income Search Icon - Opens the Transaction Search screen to find specific transactions For charts and spending insights, use Analytics from the Budget screen (pie chart icon in the top bar) or from category/section menus elsewhere in the app.

heading: Summary Card
text: At the top of the transactions list, a Summary Card shows income, expenses, and balance for the selected budget period . The totals include all budget transactions (those linked to budget categories) in that period, including both past and upcoming.

heading: Three-Column View
text: When you have both income and expenses: Income – Total money received (shown in income color) Expenses – Total money spent (shown in the app's primary color) Balance – The difference between income and expenses

heading: Visual Indicators
text: Income color = Income or positive balance Primary color = Expenses Red = Negative balance (expenses exceed income)

heading: Single-Line View
text: If you only have income or only have expenses for the selected period, the Summary Card displays a simplified single-line format showing just that information.

heading: History and Upcoming Tabs
text: When you have both past transactions and future scheduled transactions (and each section has at least some income or expenses), the screen displays two toggle buttons:

heading: History Tab
text: Shows all transactions from today and earlier, sorted with the most recent transactions first.

heading: Upcoming Tab
text: Shows all future transactions (scheduled, recurring, or planned), sorted with the soonest transactions first. Tab Information: Each tab displays the total income and expenses for that section Income is shown in income color with a "+" prefix Expenses are shown in red with a "-" prefix Tap a tab to switch between History and Upcoming views Note: If you only have past transactions or only have future transactions, the tabs won't appear—the screen will automatically show whichever section has data. Tabs also won't appear if one section has only transfers or balance adjustments (no income or expenses).

heading: Confirmation Required Block
text: If you have recurring transactions that require confirmation before being applied, they appear in a special highlighted section at the top of the transaction list. What are confirmation-required transactions? These are scheduled transactions that need your approval before they affect your account balances. This is useful for recurring expenses that may vary in amount or that you want to verify before recording. Actions: Tap a confirmation-required transaction to open options for confirming, skipping, or modifying it

heading: Transaction List
text: The list shows budget transactions for the selected budget period - that is, income and expense transactions linked to budget categories. Transactions are grouped by date with clear date headers. Each date section shows all transactions that occurred on that day. Within a day, transactions from the same receipt or the same contact may appear as a grouped row with a header - tap the group to open the full list for that receipt or contact.

heading: Transaction Display
text: Each transaction shows: Category icon (on the left) - The icon of the budget section this transaction belongs to Category name - The budget category (e.g., "Groceries", "Salary", "Rent") Amount (on the right) - The transaction amount with color coding: Income color with "+" prefix = Income Section color = Expenses (matches the category's budget section color)

heading: Additional Transaction Details
text: Transactions may also display: Receipt icon - Shown after the category name when this row belongs to a receipt. Several items from the same receipt on the same day still appear as one group. If every item in that group uses the same category, the group title is that category name with the receipt icon after it. If the items use different categories, the group title is Receipt and the icon on the left is the receipt icon. Recurring icon (↻) - Indicates this transaction is linked to a recurring template Question mark icon (?) - Indicates the transaction requires confirmation Swap icon (↔) - Indicates this is a combined transaction (categorized expense plus transfer between accounts) Contact badge - Shows which person or business this transaction involves Account badge - Shows which account was used for this transaction Description - Any notes you added to the transaction Tags - Hashtags for additional categorization (shown as #tagname)

heading: Preview Transactions
text: Future transactions from recurring templates appear slightly faded to indicate they are previews of upcoming scheduled transactions, not yet confirmed.

heading: Regular Transactions (Income/Expenses)
text: Standard income or expense transactions linked to a budget category. These are the primary transactions shown on this screen.

heading: Combined Transactions (Expense + Transfer)
text: Transactions that are both categorized expenses and transfers between accounts. These show: A swap icon (↔) indicating a transfer component The category name and icon The expense amount Note: Pure transfers between accounts, balance adjustments, and initial balances are not shown on the Transactions screen since they aren't linked to budget categories. To view those, go to the specific account's transaction history.

heading: Tap a Transaction
text: For regular transactions: Opens the Edit Transaction screen where you can modify all details. For preview/recurring transactions: Opens options to: Confirm the transaction Skip this occurrence Modify the amount or details For confirmation-required transactions: Opens a confirmation dialog with options to confirm, skip, or edit.

heading: Long-Press a Transaction
text: Long-pressing a transaction (except preview and confirmation-required ones) opens a quick actions menu with options to: Edit the transaction Edit receipt, when this transaction belongs to a receipt. Opens that receipt with all of its items, including items outside the current list Duplicate the transaction Delete the transaction Transform to receipt (for eligible expenses that are not already part of a receipt—creates a receipt from the transaction and opens the Add Receipt screen)

heading: Adding New Transactions
text: At the bottom center of the screen, a single Add Transaction floating action button opens the Add Transaction screen where you can record income or expenses. Long-press the + button at the bottom center to open Favourites . This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on Recurring Transactions ; those controls are not shown in this shortcut. To add a multi-item receipt instead, open Add Transaction in expense mode and tap the split icon next to the Category field. This opens the Add Receipt screen and carries over the selected account, date, contact, and typed amount when available. A selected category filters the store quick-select chips to contacts recently used with that category.

heading: Loading More Transactions
text: The screen initially shows a limited number of transactions for faster loading. If you have more transactions: "Show More" Button: When there are additional transactions to display, a "Show More" button appears at the bottom of the list. Tap it to load more transactions. The list always shows complete days—if you have many transactions on a single day, all of them will be shown together rather than cutting off mid-day.

heading: Empty State
text: If there are no transactions for the selected budget period, the screen displays: A receipt icon A message indicating no transactions exist for that period This is a good reminder to start recording your income and expenses!

heading: Tips for Using the Transactions Screen
text: Review regularly - Check your transactions weekly to catch any errors or forgotten entries Use the search - The search function helps you quickly find specific transactions by amount, description, or category Check upcoming transactions - Review the Upcoming tab to see what bills and income are coming up Confirm recurring transactions - Don't forget to confirm or adjust scheduled transactions that require verification Use contacts and tags - Adding contacts and tags to transactions makes it easier to filter and analyze your spending later Use receipts - From Add Transaction, use the split icon next to the category field to split one purchase into multiple categorized items Switch periods easily - Use the period picker to review past months or saved custom budget periods

The Add Transaction and Edit Transaction screens are where you record and modify your income and expense transactions. These screens provide all the fields you need to accurately track where your money goes and where it comes from.

heading: Accessing the Add Transaction Screen
text: You can open the Add Transaction screen by: Tapping the "+" button on the main Transactions screen or Budget screen Long-pressing that + button when favourites exist, then tapping a favourite in the bottom sheet. This opens a prefilled form dated today; if the template amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically. See Recurring Transactions for the shortcut and template types. Tapping "Add Transaction" from a category's menu on the Budget screen Tapping a category circle after opening a section from visual circles mode on the Budget screen (section circle → category bottom sheet → category) Using the "+" button when viewing an account's transactions Receipt split shortcut (expense mode): In expense mode, a split icon appears next to the Category field. Tap it to open the Add Receipt screen and split one purchase into multiple categorized transactions.

heading: Transaction Types
text: At the top of the Add Transaction screen, you'll see two toggle options:

heading: Expense
text: Records money going out—purchases, bills, payments. This is the default selection.

heading: Income
text: Records money coming in—salary, payments received, refunds. Tap "Income" to switch to recording income. Note: When adding transactions from a receipt, only expense mode is available since receipts typically represent purchases.

heading: Amount and Date Row
text: At the top of the form, you'll see: Amount Field: Tap to open the calculator-style number picker Enter the transaction amount The calculator supports basic math operations (+, −, ×, ÷) for splitting bills or calculating totals Your currency symbol appears next to the field This top Amount field is always the budget amount in your app's main currency (the value used by budgets, analytics, and reports) When a foreign-currency account is selected, the label can include the main currency code (for example Amount UAH ) so it stays clear which currency this field uses Date Field: Shows the transaction date in a friendly format (e.g., "Today", "Yesterday", "Mon, Jan 20") Tap to open the date picker and select a different date The date picker shows income and expense totals for each day, helping you navigate your history

heading: Confirmation Required (Future Dates Only)
text: When you set a future date, a checkbox appears: "Confirmation Required" Enable this if you want to verify the transaction before it affects your budget The transaction will appear in the "Confirmation Required" section on the Transactions screen Useful for planned expenses that might change in amount

heading: Category
text: Category Field: Shows the selected budget category with its section icon and color Tap to open the category picker Categories are organized into sections (e.g., Food, Transportation, Income) For expenses, only expense categories are shown For income, income categories are shown; you can also select expense categories for income (e.g. to record refunds or money returned to a spending category) Hidden categories within a section can be revealed with Show more (+N) ; hidden sections (not in the current period) can likewise be revealed with Show more (+N) at the bottom of the picker The category determines: Which budget the transaction counts toward The color and icon displayed for the transaction How the transaction is grouped in reports For expense transactions, the split icon next to the category field opens Add Receipt . Budgetum carries over the selected account, date, contact, and any amount already typed as the receipt total. If a category is selected, store quick-select chips on Add Receipt show contacts recently used with that category. This shortcut is hidden for income, transfers, and transactions that are already part of a receipt.

heading: Account
text: From Account / To Account Field: Shows which account this transaction uses For expenses: "From Account" (where the money comes from) For income: "To Account" (where the money goes) Tap to select from your active accounts Quick-select chips appear below the field showing your recently used accounts Required vs Optional: For regular income/expense transactions, account selection is optional. For combined transactions (transfer mode enabled), both account fields become required. If you have no active accounts, the account field is hidden and you can still save regular transactions. Recently Used Accounts: Below the account field, you may see small chips showing accounts you've used recently with this category. Tap a chip to quickly select that account. These suggestions are filtered to accounts that use the app's current main currency, so different-currency accounts are not offered as quick chips. Foreign-currency accounts (normal income/expense): You can select an account whose currency differs from the app's main currency for a regular expense or income (not only for transfers). When you do: The top Amount field remains the budget amount in the main currency An extra account amount field appears below the account picker: Expenses: Debited (money leaving the account), in the account's currency Income: Credited (money entering the account), in the account's currency Both amounts are required when currencies differ. Budgets and reports use the budget amount; the account balance moves by the debited/credited amount Budgetum may offer a market-rate quick suggestion in the number picker (based on a live rate lookup). The suggestion is optional—you can accept it or type your own amount. Rates are not saved as a separate exchange-rate history in the app Changing the account to a different currency clears the account-amount field so you can enter the new currency amount Receipts stay on the main currency: When adding or editing a receipt (or a receipt line), account selection is limited to accounts in your current main currency. Foreign-currency accounts are available for normal transactions and for multi-currency transfers, not for receipts. Transfer Toggle (↔ button): Next to the account field, you'll see a swap icon. Tap it to enable "combined transaction" mode: This records both a budget transaction AND an account transfer in one step Useful when you pay from one account but want to record money also moving to another account When enabled, additional fields appear for the transfer destination and amount If either side uses a different currency, you can enter different from/to amounts; a market-rate quick suggestion may appear in the number picker for the other side

heading: Contact
text: "Paid to" / "Received from" Field: Track who you paid or who paid you For expenses: "Paid to" (store, person, or business) For income: "Received from" (employer, client, payer) Tap to select an existing contact or create a new one Quick-select chips show recently used contacts for this category Recently Used Contacts: Below the contact field, chips appear showing contacts you've transacted with recently for this category. Tap a chip to quickly select that contact. Note: On the Add Transaction screen, this field only appears if you have the "Show contact on transaction creation" setting enabled. On the Edit Transaction screen, the contact field is always visible so you can view or change it.

heading: Description
text: Description Field: Optional. Add extra notes or details about the transaction. Examples: "Table 4", "Refund for defective item", "Bonus from Q4 review" Tap to type freely Supports multiple lines for longer notes Recently Used Descriptions: Below the description field, chips appear showing descriptions you've used before for this category. Tap anywhere inside a chip, including the space around its text, to quickly fill in that description.

heading: Tags
text: Tags Field: Add labels to organize transactions beyond categories Multiple tags can be added to a single transaction Tags appear as #tagname format Tap to open the tag selector where you can: Select existing tags Create new tags Remove selected tags Recently Used Tags: Below the tags field, chips appear showing tags you've used recently. Tap a chip to quickly add or remove that tag. Note: On the Add Transaction screen, this field only appears if you have the "Show tags on transaction creation" setting enabled. On the Edit Transaction screen, the tags field is always visible so you can view or change tags.

heading: Repeat and Favourites
text: Tap the Repeat row, arrow, or off switch to open repeat options. Turn on Favourite at the top to save a reusable template without needing a schedule. When no favourite templates are saved, a small, muted helper beneath the switch explains that favourites let you quickly add transactions without a repeat schedule. It is hidden when you open Repeat with at least one saved favourite. The switch keeps the page open; Back retains the choice in the transaction form. Selecting Do not repeat or a repeat preset returns immediately with the favourite choice preserved. Custom opens a separate schedule page; applying it also preserves Favourite. Favourite only: turn on Favourite, leave Do not repeat selected, return and save the transaction. No automatic transactions are generated. Favourite and scheduled: turn on Favourite, select a daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or custom schedule, then save. Scheduled only: choose a schedule with Favourite off, as before. A small filled star beside the Repeat field name shows that the template is a favourite. There is no extra favourite subtitle; schedule details remain in the existing helper below the field when repetition is enabled. The switch controls automatic repetition and stays off for favourite-only templates. Switching repetition off keeps the favourite mark. End conditions (never, date or occurrence count) appear only with a schedule, along with a next-transaction date control where supported. Changes are saved only when you save the transaction form. Availability and Pro: Repeat is not offered when adding receipt items or a transaction from a template, or when editing a transaction already linked to a template. For linked transactions, edit the template from Recurring Transactions instead. All saved templates, including favourite-only and inactive templates, share the existing free limit of five; Pro allows unlimited templates. At the limit, tapping the Pro-marked Repeat field opens the upgrade page. Open Recurring Transactions → Favourites to use saved favourites. This is the first filter and opens by default when favourites exist; otherwise All opens. Drag row handles to save a manual order, or tap a row for Add Transaction, Add to Favourites or Remove from Favourites, Edit, and Delete. See Recurring Transactions for detailed steps.

heading: Search History Button
text: At the bottom center of the screen, a floating search button opens Transaction History Search: Search through your past transactions Select a previous transaction to copy its details (category, description, amount, contact, tags) Great for quickly entering similar transactions

heading: Smart Suggestions
text: The app learns from your habits and suggests: Contacts you frequently use with the selected category Descriptions you've used before Accounts you typically use with each category Account suggestions are limited to accounts in your current main currency. Manage notes and description suggestions On Add Transaction, Edit Transaction, and the receipt item form, long-press a description suggestion below the Description field to open a bottom sheet: Hide this suggestion hides that exact description in the selected category. Hide all suggestions in this category hides every description currently suggested for that category, including suggestions beyond the visible chips or excluded by the text you have typed. The category name appears below the action. Other categories are unaffected. New descriptions can still appear later; using an already hidden description again does not unhide it. Manage notes opens a page for the selected category, with the category name in the app bar. When a category is selected and the Description field is empty (or contains only spaces), tap the three-dot button on its right to open the same menu without Hide this suggestion , even when no chips remain. The button is hidden when no category is selected or when you enter a note. The document icon on the left is decorative and has no long-press action. There is no additional settings item. Hiding takes effect immediately, without a confirmation dialog. It does not change the current Description field or any saved transaction notes. You can still type hidden descriptions manually. Hidden choices are remembered across app launches and apply to both Add and Edit Transaction. When opened from a receipt item, the same controls also include notes from items already added to that receipt; see Receipt descriptions for draft-note behavior. Manage notes starts on the Visible tab, showing each distinct, nonempty description used by transactions in the category that has not been hidden. Repeated transaction descriptions appear only once. The Hidden tab shows descriptions hidden in that category. Rows show only the description and its action icon: On Visible , tap the hide (crossed-out eye) icon to hide that description. It leaves Visible and becomes available in Hidden. On Hidden , tap the restore icon to unhide the description. It leaves Hidden and returns to Visible if a transaction in the category still uses it. Tapping the description or the rest of the row does nothing. Neither action inserts text into the transaction form or edits saved notes. Tap the search icon at the top right to expand Search notes inside the app bar. Search filters descriptions in the current tab (case-insensitive), across the entire category, including records not yet loaded. Switching tabs keeps the search text. Tap the search-off icon in the app bar to close search and clear the filter. Each tab initially loads up to 100 descriptions, sorted by description. Scroll to the bottom and tap Load more to load the next 100; the button disappears when every matching result is loaded. Changing or closing search, or switching tabs, starts again with the first 100 results. Tap the three-dot button at the top right for bulk actions: On Visible , Hide all (N) hides every visible description in the category. With a nonempty search, Hide filtered (N) hides only matching descriptions. On Hidden , Restore all (N) restores every hidden description in the category. With a nonempty search, Restore filtered (N) restores only matching descriptions. N is the complete matching record count, not the number of loaded rows or transactions. For example, searching “coffee” on Hidden and selecting Restore filtered (105) restores all 105 matching descriptions even if only 100 are loaded.
