Bulk actions run immediately without confirmation; other categories and saved transaction notes are unchanged. Search text and the selected tab remain in place. The bulk action is disabled when its count is zero. The three-dot and row action buttons are disabled while results load or an action is running; search and tab switching are disabled while a hide or restore is running. The page shows a loading spinner while opening or changing filters, No visible notes or No hidden suggestions when the current tab has no records, or No matching suggestions when records exist in that tab but none match the search. Use Back to return to the transaction form; entered values are preserved and suggestions are refreshed. A restored suggestion appears when the category and typed text match, subject to the usual limit of ten visible chips. To manage another category, return to the form, select that category, and open Manage notes again.

heading: Single Save Mode
text: When you open Add Transaction from a category tap: Tap the checkmark (✓) to save and close The transaction is saved and you return to the previous screen

heading: Multi-Entry Mode
text: When you open Add Transaction from the main + button: Tap the checkmark (✓) to save A "Transaction added" confirmation appears The form clears so you can quickly add another transaction The category stays selected for faster entry of multiple items in the same category

heading: Accessing Edit Transaction
text: Open the Edit Transaction screen by: Tapping any transaction in your transaction list Tapping "Edit" from a transaction's options menu

heading: What You Can Change
text: All fields can be edited: Amount and date Category Account(s) Contact Description Tags Recurring settings (for transactions not yet linked to a recurring template)

heading: Edit Screen Notes
text: Contact and tags: The contact and tags fields are always visible when editing (they are not hidden by the "Show contact on transaction creation" or "Show tags on transaction creation" settings). Quick suggestions: Description suggestion chips appear when editing, same as on Add. Recently used contact and account chips are only shown on the Add Transaction screen. Foreign-currency transactions: If the transaction uses a foreign-currency account, edit shows the saved budget amount and the saved Debited/Credited account amount. Changing either amount updates that stored value; Budgetum does not rewrite historical amounts from a live rate. Combined transactions (transfers): When editing a combined transaction, account selection is limited to accounts in your app's current currency. Different-currency transfers can be created on the Add screen; when editing, you can still change amounts but the account picker will only offer accounts in the current currency. Receipt lines: The amount is the unit price, and an Items Count field sits beside it. Budgets and the account use unit price × count. Changing the count updates only this line. Duplicate copies the unit price into a new transaction dated today; the copy is not part of the receipt and its count is 1. Account selection stays on the main currency.

heading: Also update recurring template amount
text: When editing a transaction that is linked to a recurring template, and you change the budget amount (or the foreign-currency Debited/Credited amount), a checkbox appears: Also update recurring template amount Leave it off to change only this occurrence. Check it to also write the new amount(s) back to the recurring template so future generated occurrences use the updated template amount. The same checkbox appears when editing a linked transfer or balance adjustment from their edit screens.

heading: Additional Edit Options
text: The three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right provides extra options: Change to income / Change to expense: Switches the transaction between income and expense The title area shows an Income or Expense badge for the current type; this menu is how you change it (there is no type toggle on Edit) Hidden for receipt-linked items Switching type swaps the from and to accounts If you switch to expense and the current category is an income category, the category is cleared and you must select a category before saving Switching to income keeps an expense category (for refunds or money returned to a spending category) The Also update recurring template amount checkbox is hidden while the edited type differs from the linked template’s type Edit receipt: Shown when this transaction belongs to a receipt Opens that receipt with all of its items, including items that are not this line When you leave the receipt, you return to the list, not this transaction editor Transform to Receipt: Converts a single expense transaction into a multi-item receipt Useful when you realize a transaction should be split across multiple categories Only available for expense transactions that are not already part of a receipt and are not combined transfers (the source account, if any, must also use your main currency) Duplicate: Creates a copy of the transaction with today's date All other details are preserved Opens as a new Add Transaction screen with the values pre-filled Delete: Permanently removes the transaction You'll be asked to confirm before deletion This action cannot be undone

heading: Update Similar Transactions
text: When you change a description, a checkbox may appear: "Update X similar transactions" If you have other transactions with the same original description Check this box to update all of them to the new description Useful for fixing typos or improving consistency

heading: Combined Transactions (Transfer + Budget)
text: For advanced tracking, you can create a combined transaction that: Records a budget transaction (expense or income to a category) Records an account transfer at the same time

heading: How to Enable
text: Select an account in the "From Account" field Tap the swap icon (↔) next to the account field A second account field appears for the transfer destination

heading: Transfer Amount
text: When creating a combined transaction, you can select accounts with different currencies: You can enter different amounts for each side The number picker may offer a market-rate quick suggestion between the two account currencies This handles exchange rate differences without storing a permanent rate table When editing an existing transaction, account selection is limited to your app's current currency (see "Edit Screen Notes" under Editing Transactions).

heading: When to Use
text: Combined transactions are helpful when: You receive income into one of your accounts and want to record the transfer You record savings as an expense and transfer to your savings account You want to track both the category spending and the money movement

heading: Tips for Adding Transactions
text: Add transactions promptly - Record expenses right after they happen while details are fresh Use the search feature - The history search helps you quickly find and copy past transactions Be consistent with descriptions - Use similar descriptions for similar transactions to make searching easier Assign contacts - Linking transactions to contacts helps you analyze spending by store or person Use tags for special tracking - Tags let you track things across categories (like vacation expenses) Check the date - Make sure the date is correct, especially when entering transactions from receipts or statements Set up recurring transactions - Save time by setting up repeating bills and income once Use quick-select chips - The suggestion chips below fields speed up entry significantly Review before saving - Double-check the amount and category before tapping save Foreign-currency spending - For a USD card with a UAH budget (for example), enter the real card charge as Debited/Credited and the budget value as Amount so reports stay in your main currency

Receipts in Budgetum let you record multiple purchases from a single shopping trip or invoice as individual transactions. Instead of creating one transaction for your entire grocery bill, you can split it into categories like groceries, household supplies, and snacks—giving you more accurate insights into where your money actually goes.

heading: Accessing the Add Receipt Screen
text: You can open the Add Receipt screen by: Opening Add Transaction in expense mode and tapping the split icon next to the Category field Using the Add Receipt option from an account's transaction view Converting an existing transaction to a receipt via the Edit Transaction menu When opened from Add Transaction, Budgetum carries over the selected account, date, contact, and any amount already typed as the receipt total. A selected category is used only to filter store suggestions; it is not applied to receipt items.

heading: How Receipts Work
text: A receipt in Budgetum is a collection of items that all share the same: Date - When the purchase happened Account - Which account you paid from Contact - The store or business where you shopped Each item within the receipt can have its own: Amount - How much that item cost Category - Which budget category it belongs to Description - What the item was Tags - Additional labels for organization This lets you accurately categorize a single shopping trip across multiple budget categories.

heading: Total and Date Row
text: At the top of the form: Total Field: Enter the total amount from your receipt Tap to open the calculator-style number picker This is the target amount—your item totals should match this The app will alert you if your items don't add up to the total Date Field: Shows the receipt date Tap to open the date picker All items on this receipt will use this date

heading: Account Selection
text: From Account Field: Select which account you paid from Tap to open the account picker (only accounts in your current main currency are available; foreign-currency accounts cannot be used on receipts) Use the clear button (×) to clear the selection Quick-select chips appear below showing recently used accounts in your current main currency (chips may be hidden when you have only one default account and it is already selected) This account will be applied to all items on the receipt. The account section is only shown when you have at least one active account.

heading: Contact Selection
text: "Paid to" (Payment Recipient) Field: Select the store or business where you made the purchase Tap to open the contact picker, or tap a chip to select a recent contact (tap again to clear) Quick-select chips show recently used contacts. When Add Receipt was opened from Add Transaction with a category selected, the chips show contacts recently used with that category. Opening the contact picker uses the same category for its suggestions. This contact will be applied to all items on the receipt. Note: This field only appears if you have the "Show contact on transaction creation" setting enabled.

heading: Items List
text: Below the header fields, you'll see: "Add Item" Button: Tap to add a new item to the receipt Opens the Add Receipt Item screen Items Card: Lists all items you've added Each item shows: Category name and icon Description (if provided) Tags (if assigned) Quantity badge (if more than 1) Amount in the category's color Tap any item to edit it

heading: Balance Indicator
text: At the bottom of the screen, a colored bar appears when your items don't match the total: "Remaining: $XX.XX" (Blue) Your items total less than the receipt total The remaining amount needs to be assigned to items Tap "Fix" to quickly add an item for the remaining amount "Excess: $XX.XX" (Red) Your items total more than the receipt total You've added more than the receipt amount Tap "Fix" to automatically adjust the total to match your items The save button only appears when your items exactly match the receipt total. Closing the screen: Tap the close (×) button to leave. If the total, date, account, contact, or items differ from when you opened the receipt, the app asks whether to discard your changes. An unchanged receipt closes immediately.

heading: Adding Receipt Items
text: When you tap "Add Item", the Add Receipt Item screen opens with these fields:

heading: Amount and Count Row
text: Amount Field: The price of this item Tap to open the calculator number picker Enter the unit price if buying multiples Items Count Field: How many of this item you bought Defaults to 1 The field is read-only; tap it to open the Number Picker (titled Items Count ) Must be a positive whole number (1, 2, 3, …). You cannot type a count freely, and decimals or zero are rejected Increase for multiples (e.g., 3 bottles of water) The total for this line will be amount × count Price Suggestions: When you have a category (or description) entered and have more than one previous price for similar transactions, price chips appear below the amount field. Tap a chip to quickly select that price.

heading: Category
text: Category Field: Select which budget category this item belongs to Only expense categories are shown (receipts are for expenses) The category's icon and color help you identify it If you've already added items, the last-used category is remembered

heading: Description
text: Description Field: Describe what this item is Examples: "Milk 2%", "Birthday candles", "Paper towels" Helps you remember what the purchase was for Supports multiple lines for longer notes Description Suggestions: After you select a category, up to ten chips appear below showing descriptions from saved transactions and items already added to the current receipt in that category, excluding hidden notes. The list is filtered as you type. Tap anywhere inside a chip, including the space around its text, to fill the Description field and refresh suggested prices. When adding or editing a receipt item, long-press a description chip to open the usual bottom sheet: Hide this suggestion hides that exact note in this category. Hide all suggestions in this category hides all current notes in the category, including notes from other unsaved items in this receipt and notes beyond the visible chips. It does not use the text currently typed in the Description field as a filter. Manage notes opens the selected category’s notes page. When a category is selected and the Description field is empty (or contains only spaces), tap its right-hand three-dot button to open the same menu without Hide this suggestion . This remains available after all chips are hidden. The button is hidden when no category is selected or when you enter a note. The document icon on the left is decorative and has no long-press action. Manage notes has Visible and Hidden toggles and starts on Visible. Visible includes distinct notes from saved transactions and other items already added to this receipt; duplicates appear only once. Hidden includes the category’s hidden notes. The category name appears in the app bar. Tap the hide icon on a Visible row or the restore icon on a Hidden row; tapping the row text does nothing. Restoring a draft-only note returns it to Visible while it is still present in this receipt. Use the search icon in the app bar to open Search notes . It searches the current view across all records, including unloaded ones. Switching Visible/Hidden keeps the search text; the search-off icon clears it. Notes load in batches of 100 with Load more at the bottom. Switching views or changing search returns to the first batch. The three-dot menu offers Hide all (N) on Visible and Restore all (N) on Hidden. With a nonempty search, these become Hide filtered (N) and Restore filtered (N) . N counts all matching distinct notes, including unloaded notes and, on Visible, draft receipt notes. Actions run immediately without confirmation and affect only this category. Zero-count actions are disabled; loading or an ongoing action temporarily disables controls. Use Back to return to the receipt item. Its entered description, amount, quantity, category, and tags are preserved, and suggestion chips refresh. Hiding or restoring never edits saved transaction notes or receipt items. Hidden choices are shared with Add/Edit Transaction and remain saved even if you cancel the receipt; a hidden draft-only note can be restored from Hidden later, but appears in Visible only if a saved transaction or the current receipt still contains it. Price suggestions and receipt history search remain available independently of hidden description chips. See Manage notes and description suggestions for empty states and detailed shared controls.

heading: Tags
text: Tags Field: Add labels to this specific item Useful for tracking specific purposes (e.g., "Party supplies") Multiple tags can be selected Tag Suggestions: Chips show your recently used tags for quick selection. Note: The tags field only appears if you have the "Show tags on transaction creation" setting enabled.

heading: Saving Items
text: Add Another (✓ button): When adding a new item, tap the checkmark to save and add another The form clears but keeps your category (and tags) selected for the next item A confirmation message appears briefly Continue adding items until you've entered everything Save Edit: When editing an existing item, tap the checkmark to save changes You return to the receipt screen Delete (trash icon): Only appears when editing an existing item Removes the item from the receipt

heading: Remaining / excess bar (adding an item)
text: When you are adding a new item (not editing one) and the receipt has a total greater than zero, a bar at the bottom of the item screen shows how the already-added items compare with that total: Remaining: $XX.XX The added items total less than the receipt total Tap Add remaining to fill the amount with the leftover and set Items Count to 1. You still choose a category (and other fields) and save the item with the checkmark. Excess: $XX.XX The added items total more than the receipt total No action button is shown on this bar Save receipt Appears on the bar when the added items already match the receipt total exactly Saves the whole receipt from the item screen using the items already added; it does not add the item you are currently typing After a successful save, you leave the receipt This bar is hidden when you are editing an existing item, or when the receipt has no total yet.

heading: Search History
text: At the bottom of the Add Receipt Item screen, a floating search button opens the Receipt History Search: How it works: Search through your past transactions Find items you've purchased before Select a result to copy its category, description, and amount Great for items you buy regularly When you have a contact selected on the receipt, the search prioritizes transactions with that contact, making it easy to find items you've bought at that store before.

heading: Editing, Duplicating, and Deleting a Saved Receipt
text: Long-press a receipt group in a transaction list to open Edit , Duplicate , and Delete . These actions are also available from the receipt's transaction group page. Long-press a single receipt item, including on category, section, contact, and tag lists where items are not grouped, and choose Edit receipt . The same action is in the three-dot menu on Edit Transaction for that item. It opens the receipt with all of its items. From Edit Transaction, leaving the receipt returns you to the list. Edit opens the same form used to create a receipt, with all its items loaded even when the transaction list is filtered. Change the date, account, contact, or individual items; add items, remove items, or change quantities. The item total must match the receipt total before saving. Changes stay in the form until you save. Saving updates the receipt and account balances together, preserving existing transaction identities where possible. Closing with no changes leaves immediately. If you changed the receipt, the app asks before discarding. Cancelling leaves the saved receipt untouched. Duplicate opens a new receipt draft with the original items and today's date. Delete asks for confirmation before removing the entire receipt and all its transactions.

heading: Editing Receipt Items
text: Tap any item in the items list to: Change its amount, count, category, description, or tags Delete the item from the receipt Changes take effect immediately when you save.

heading: Saving the Receipt
text: The save button (✓) in the top-right corner only appears when: You have at least one item Your items' total exactly matches the receipt total When you save: Each item line becomes one transaction. Its amount is the line total (unit price × count), and the count is stored on that transaction Identical lines stay separate. Count is not combined across lines All transactions share the same date, account, and contact Each transaction goes to its respective category The items are linked together as a receipt group

heading: Converting a Transaction to a Receipt
text: If you've already recorded a single transaction but want to split it: Open the transaction for editing Tap the three-dot menu (⋮) Select "Transform to Receipt" The receipt screen opens with the amount and contact pre-filled Add individual items to break down the purchase The original transaction is replaced when you save Use this when: You recorded a quick total but want more detail later You realize a purchase spans multiple categories You have time to properly categorize a shopping trip

heading: Viewing Receipt History
text: Receipts appear in your transaction history like regular transactions, but: On Transactions, account lists, and sets, items from the same receipt on the same day are grouped together. If they all use one category, the group title is that category name with a receipt icon after it. If they use different categories, the group title is Receipt and the icon on the left is the receipt icon. Category, section, contact, tag, and similar lists show each item on its own. A receipt icon after the category name (or after the description, when the category name is hidden) means that line belongs to a receipt. The receipt's total contact badge shows on all items Each item shows its category and line total. When the count is greater than 1, the line also shows ×N Tip: Tap any receipt item to view and edit just that item, or view the contact to see all transactions at that store.

heading: Tips for Using Receipts
text: Enter the total first - Start with the receipt total so you know when you've accounted for everything Use the search feature - The history search finds items you've bought before, saving time on repeat purchases Keep it simple - You don't need to itemize everything; group small similar items together Use descriptions - Brief descriptions like "produce" or "cleaning supplies" help you remember later Check your math - The balance indicator helps ensure you don't miss or double-count items Set the contact - Linking to a store lets you analyze spending by location over time Add items as you go - You can add items, return to the receipt, and add more without losing progress Use the count field - For multiples of the same item at the same price, use count instead of adding separate items Let suggestions help - The price and description suggestions from your history speed up entry significantly

heading: Example: Grocery Store Receipt
text: Here's how you might enter a grocery store receipt: Receipt header: Total $87.54, date today, account Checking Account, contact Supermart. Items you add: Groceries — Fruits and vegetables, $23.45 × 1 Groceries — Dairy (milk 2%), $6.50 × 2 → $13.00 Groceries — Meat, $28.50 × 1 Household — Paper products, $8.99 × 1 Health — Vitamins, $13.60 × 1 The milk line uses count 2 so you enter one line (price × 2) instead of two separate lines. Your item total matches the receipt total, so the save button appears. When you save, you get five transactions, one per line. The milk transaction is $13.00 with count 2, shown as ×2 in the receipt's transaction list. The others are one each at their line amount. All share the same date, account, and contact, each in its category.

The Recurring Transactions Screen manages saved transaction templates: scheduled subscriptions, bills and income, plus favourites you reuse manually. A template can be a favourite, have an automatic repeat schedule, or both. Favourites use the same transaction details as other templates; there is no separate template-name field.

heading: Accessing the Recurring Screen
text: You can access the Recurring Transactions Screen by: Tapping the repeat icon (↻) in the top bar of the Transactions screen Going to More → Advanced Features → Recurring Transactions

heading: Understanding Recurring Transactions
text: Templates with an active repeat schedule automatically create transactions on that schedule. Marking a template as Favourite alone does not enable automatic repetition. Common examples include: Subscriptions - Netflix, Spotify, gym memberships Bills - Rent, utilities, phone bills, insurance Regular Income - Salary, freelance payments, rental income Scheduled Transfers - Regular savings transfers, investment contributions Recurring Fees - Bank fees, service charges Scheduled templates generate transactions on their scheduled dates. Favourite-only templates wait for you to choose Add Transaction from their options.

heading: Filter Bar
text: At the top of the screen, you'll find filter buttons to quickly narrow down which recurring transactions to display: Favourites - The first filter; shows all templates marked as Favourite, whether scheduled or not, in your saved manual order All - Shows all templates (active and inactive, including favourites) Day - Only templates that repeat daily Week - Only templates that repeat weekly Month - Only templates that repeat monthly Year - Only templates that repeat yearly Not Active - Templates that have been saved but don't have an active recurrence schedule When you open this screen, Favourites is selected if at least one favourite exists; otherwise All is selected. Tap any filter to switch the view. The selected filter is highlighted. Updates while the screen is open preserve your chosen filter. A scheduled favourite also appears in All and its matching frequency filter; a favourite without a schedule also appears in All and Not Active.

heading: Search
text: Tap the search icon in the top right corner to find specific recurring transactions (tap again to close search). You can search by: Template description or notes Category name Budget section name Amount Account name (source or destination) Contact name Tags Recurrence pattern (e.g., "monthly", "weekly") When searching, matching templates are displayed while non-matching ones are hidden.

heading: Pro Version Banner
text: If you're using the free version of Budgetum, you'll see a banner at the top of the list indicating that the free tier is limited to 5 recurring transaction templates. The banner is hidden while search is open or when a search query is active. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited templates. Favourite-only, scheduled and inactive templates all count toward the same five-template free limit. A template that is both a favourite and scheduled counts once. Favourites do not receive a separate free allowance. At the limit, the Repeat field for creating a new template shows a Pro badge and opens the upgrade page; existing templates remain editable.

heading: Favourites List and Manual Order
text: Favourites appear as a flat list without date groups. Drag the small dotted grip at the left of a row to move it; the new order is saved immediately and remains after reopening the app. A template you newly mark as a favourite is added at the end of the list. Reordering is available only in Favourites. When a search query is entered, the drag handles are hidden; clear the query to reorder again. If saving the order fails, an error message appears and the list reloads its saved order. Tap a favourite anywhere in its main row to open the same options as other templates: Add Transaction , Remove from Favourites , Edit , and Delete . Reordering does not change its schedule or transaction details. Backups preserve favourite marks and saved ordering.

heading: Active Templates (Grouped by Next Date)
text: Outside the Favourites filter, active recurring templates are organized by their next scheduled occurrence date. Each date group shows: Calendar icon and date - When the next occurrence will happen (displayed in a friendly format like "Today", "Tomorrow", "Monday", or the full date) Total amount - The net amount for that date: income minus expenses. It shows a "+" when income is larger (for example, a $3,200 paycheck and $1,850 rent on the same day show +$1,350 ) and no sign when expenses are larger. Transfers and balance adjustments are not counted, and the total is hidden when the net is zero Below each date header, you'll see the individual templates grouped under that date.

heading: Template Display
text: Each recurring template shows the following information: Main Row: Category icon (on the left) - The icon of the budget section this template belongs to Category or title - The name of the category, or for transfers and balance adjustments, a descriptive title. Outside the Favourites filter, a filled star after the name means the template is a favourite. The star is hidden on Favourites, where every row is already a favourite Amount (on the right) - The template amount with color coding: "+" prefix and income color = Income (uses your budget's Income section color) Section color = Expenses (matches the category's budget section color) Additional Details (when applicable): Contact badge - Shows which person or business this recurring transaction involves Account badge - Shows which account is used Description - Any notes you added to the template Tags - Hashtags for additional categorization (shown as #tagname) Recurrence label - Shown only for active schedules. Inactive templates, including favourites without a schedule, have no recurrence label. A description of the active schedule (e.g., "Every month", "Every 2 weeks", "Every Monday", "1st and 15th of the month")

heading: Inactive Templates Section
text: Templates that have been saved without an active recurrence schedule appear in two ways: When "Not Active" is selected – Only inactive templates are shown (no date groups). When "All" is selected – Active templates appear first, grouped by next date; inactive templates are listed at the bottom under a "Not Active" header. Frequency filters (Day, Week, Month, Year) show active schedules only. When "Favourites" is selected – Inactive favourites appear alongside scheduled favourites in your manual order. These are useful for: Templates you've paused temporarily One-time templates you might want to reactivate later Drafts you haven't fully configured yet The inactive section has a "Not Active" header and displays templates with a different visual styling.

heading: Regular Recurring Transactions
text: Standard income or expense templates linked to a budget category. These are the most common type—things like your monthly rent, weekly grocery budget, or salary.

heading: Recurring Transfers
text: Templates for regular money movement between your accounts. Transfer templates show: A swap icon (↔) indicating a transfer The source and destination accounts with an arrow between them The transfer amount Common uses: monthly savings transfers, regular investment contributions, credit card payments.

heading: Recurring Balance Adjustments
text: Templates for regular balance corrections. These show: "Balance Increase" or "Balance Decrease" as the title A plus or minus icon indicating the adjustment direction The affected account Common uses: recurring bank fees, regular interest payments, scheduled adjustments.

heading: Quick access from Budget and Transactions
text: When Favourites is selected and the list is not empty, a small hint below the filters explains: Hold + on Budget or Transactions to add from favourites. Tap its × button to dismiss it. The hint also disappears after you first open the favourites shortcut sheet, even if you close that sheet without adding a transaction. This is remembered after restarting the app. More → Reset Tutorial restores the hint, including after you have already used the shortcut. The hint is not shown in other filters or when there are no matching favourites. Long-press the + button at the bottom center to open Favourites . This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on Recurring Transactions ; those controls are not shown in this shortcut. This shortcut uses the existing favourites and does not require a separate Pro upgrade. Creating templates remains subject to the shared free limit described above. Creating a manual transaction from a scheduled favourite does not change its repeat schedule. Zero-amount templates also open the number picker when you choose Add Transaction from this screen.

heading: Template options
text: Tap a recurring template in the list to open an options sheet with: Add Transaction — create a one-off transaction prefilled from the template (category, amount, accounts, contact and tags where applicable), using today’s date. Review or change the details and save to create the transaction. The new transaction stays associated with the template for history and reporting. Add to Favourites or Remove from Favourites — mark or unmark the template immediately. The label matches its current state. This does not delete the template or change its schedule, amount, accounts, or other details. A newly added favourite appears at the end of the list. Adding it again after you remove it also places it at the end. The list updates as soon as you choose the option. Edit — open the Edit Template screen Delete — remove the template (existing transactions created from it are kept) Opening the options sheet does not create a transaction. The Add Transaction subtitle explains that it creates a transaction from the template. Choosing Add to Favourites or Remove from Favourites closes the sheet and saves that change; you do not need to open Edit or save the template again.

heading: Editing a Template
text: From the options sheet, choose Edit to open Edit Template . For regular income or expense templates, the title area shows an Income or Expense badge. Transfers and balance-adjustment templates do not show this badge. The three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right includes: Change to income / Change to expense: Switches the template between income and expense Not shown for transfer or balance-adjustment templates Switching type swaps the from and to accounts If you switch to expense and the current category is an income category, the category is cleared and you must select a category before saving Delete is also in this menu (see Deleting a Template ). Transaction Details: Amount and Start Date - The template budget amount and when the recurrence begins Category - The budget category (for regular transactions) Accounts - Source and/or destination accounts Foreign-currency amounts - If the primary account uses a currency different from the app's main currency, an extra Debited / Credited field appears for the account-side amount (same idea as Add/Edit Transaction). Occurrences copy both the budget amount and the account amount; no live rate lookup runs during generation Update from an occurrence - When you edit a transaction already linked to this template and change its amount, Edit Transaction can offer Also update recurring template amount so future occurrences pick up the new template amount → Add/Edit Transaction Contact - The person or business involved Description - Notes about this recurring transaction Tags - Any tags for organization Recurrence Settings: Favourite - From the template options, choose Add to Favourites or Remove from Favourites . That change is saved immediately and does not delete the template or change its schedule. You can also open Repeat while editing and turn Favourite on or off; that choice is saved when you save the template. Recurrence pattern - How often and when the template repeats Options include: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom schedules You can set specific days of the week, days of the month, or create complex patterns Transaction History: Below the form, you'll see a list of actual transactions that have been created from this template This helps you verify that the recurring transaction is working correctly Tap "Show More" to load additional history

heading: Saving Changes
text: Tap the checkmark (✓) in the top right corner to save your changes. The template will be updated and future occurrences will use the new settings.

heading: Deleting a Template
text: Open the three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right and choose Delete . You'll be asked to confirm before the template is permanently deleted. Note: Deleting a template does not delete transactions that were already created from it. Those transactions remain in your history.

heading: Recurrence Options
text: Budgetum supports flexible scheduling for recurring transactions:

heading: Common Presets
text: Daily - Every day Weekly - Every week on the same day Every 2 Weeks - Bi-weekly Monthly - Every month on the same date Yearly - Once a year on the same date

heading: Custom Schedules
text: For more complex needs, you can create custom recurrence patterns: Specific weekdays - Every Monday and Wednesday Specific days of the month - The 1st and 15th of each month Nth weekday - The first Monday of each month, the last Friday Multiple months - Only in certain months of the year Custom intervals - Every 3 weeks, every 6 months, etc.

heading: Schedule Limits
text: You can optionally set: End date - Stop the recurrence after a specific date Maximum occurrences - Stop after a certain number of transactions

heading: No Recurring Transactions
text: If you haven't set up any recurring transactions yet, or when the current filter has no matching templates (for example, you have only inactive templates and filter by "Month"), the screen displays: A repeat icon A message indicating you have no recurring transactions This is a great time to set up your regular bills and income!

heading: No Favourites
text: If Favourites is selected but contains no templates, the screen says: No favourites yet. Tap a template in another filter and choose Add to Favourites. This can happen after removing the last favourite while this filter is open. Switch to All or another filter, tap a template, and choose Add to Favourites . You can also mark a template as Favourite in Repeat options while editing it. On the next visit with no favourites, All opens by default.

heading: No Search Results
text: When searching, if no templates match your query: An empty-results icon appears A message indicates no results were found Try adjusting your search terms or clearing the search.

heading: Creating Recurring Transactions
text: To save a favourite, a schedule, or both: Open Add Transaction and fill in its details, or edit a transaction that is not already linked to a template. The same Repeat control is available in transfer and balance-adjustment forms when template creation is allowed. Tap Repeat (the repeat icon/row, its arrow, or its switch when off) to open the options page. Turn on the Favourite switch at the top. When no favourite templates are saved, a small, muted helper beneath the switch explains that favourites let you quickly add transactions without a repeat schedule. It is hidden when you open Repeat with at least one saved favourite. Turning it on or off keeps the options page open and retains the choice in the parent form. For a favourite without a schedule, leave Do not repeat selected and use Back, or tap Do not repeat to return. For a scheduled favourite, select a repeat preset: the page returns immediately with both choices. Custom opens custom schedule settings; applying them also returns with the favourite mark preserved. Back in the form, a small filled star beside the Repeat field name identifies a favourite. There is no extra favourite subtitle; the existing schedule helper remains below the field when repetition is enabled. The switch represents automatic repetition: it stays off for favourite-only templates. Turning it off preserves the favourite mark but disables repetition. End and next-transaction controls are shown only when a schedule is enabled (the next-date control is available in forms that support it). Save the transaction or, when editing a template, tap the top-right checkmark. Returning from Repeat only updates the form; leaving the parent form without saving does not save those changes. The template appears in Favourites if marked. Scheduled templates also appear in their frequency filter. To mark an existing template, tap it in any filter and choose Add to Favourites . To remove it, tap it and choose Remove from Favourites . Either choice is saved immediately; the template remains in All, and any active schedule continues. You can still change the favourite mark from Edit → Repeat, which is saved when you save the template. Repeat is unavailable when adding receipt items or creating a transaction from a template, and is hidden when editing a transaction already linked to a template. Use Edit on the template itself to change its favourite mark or schedule. Favourite templates share the existing Pro limits described above.

heading: Automatic Generation
text: Budgetum automatically generates transactions from your templates based on their schedule: The template tracks the "next occurrence" date When that date arrives (or passes), a planned transaction is created and appears in your Transactions list The transaction appears on your budget and in the Transactions list, and is marked as requiring confirmation: you can approve it (to clear the flag), edit and approve, or delete it. After you approve, account balances are updated to reflect the transaction. After each occurrence, the next date is calculated based on your recurrence pattern

heading: Confirmation Required Block
text: Transactions generated from recurring templates (and any other planned transactions that require confirmation) appear in the Confirmation Required block at the top of the Transactions screen. They are also included in your budget totals and shown on the Budget screen. The block can be expanded or collapsed. From there you can approve a transaction (to clear the confirmation flag), edit it and then approve, or delete it. After you approve, account balances are updated to reflect the transaction.

heading: Missed Occurrences
text: If you don't open the app for a while, Budgetum catches up by generating any missed occurrences. Past-due recurring transactions will appear in your history with their correct dates.

heading: Tips for Managing Recurring Transactions
text: Set up all your bills - Enter your rent, utilities, subscriptions, and regular expenses so nothing gets forgotten Include regular income - Add your salary, freelance payments, or other regular income sources Use descriptive names - Add descriptions to templates so you remember what each one is for (e.g., "Netflix subscription", "Monthly gym fee") Review regularly - Check the Recurring screen periodically to update canceled subscriptions or changed amounts Use the filters - If you have many recurring items, use the frequency filters to focus on specific types Check transaction history - Use the history in the edit screen to verify that transactions are being created correctly Set appropriate accounts - Link each recurring transaction to the correct account so your balances stay accurate Use contacts - Add contacts to recurring transactions to track who you pay or receive money from regularly Foreign-currency templates - For subscriptions charged in another currency, set both the budget amount and the account Debited/Credited amount on the template so generated occurrences stay correct without needing the network Pause instead of delete - If you temporarily stop a subscription, you can remove the recurrence without deleting the template, making it easy to reactivate later Use the Confirmation Required block - Recurring-generated transactions appear there until you approve them; you can edit the amount (or other details) before confirming if needed

The Day Transactions Screen provides a focused view of your transactions for a specific day, with an integrated calendar for easy navigation between dates. This screen helps you review daily spending patterns and see exactly what happened on any given day.

heading: Accessing the Day Transactions Screen
text: You can access the Day Transactions Screen by: Main Transactions screen — Tapping the calendar icon in the app bar Account, category, or other entity — When viewing transactions for an account, category, section, contact, or tag, tapping the calendar icon in the period bar (the bar below the header that shows the date range) opens the Day Transactions Screen for that same entity

heading: Top Bar (Header)
text: The top bar stays visible while you scroll. It displays the currently selected date and provides quick navigation controls. Elements: Left Arrow (<) - Navigate to the previous day Selected Date - Shows the current date in a friendly format (e.g., "Today", "Yesterday", "Mon, Jan 20") Daily Total - Displays the net total for the selected day (income minus expenses). Shown only when the day has transactions or when in selection mode with at least one transaction selected. Right Arrow (>) - Navigate to the next day Selection Mode Button - Toggle multi-select mode for transactions (checkmark icon). Hidden for future dates. Actions: Tap the date or calendar icon beside it to scroll back to the calendar at the top of the page. This preserves the selected day and any selected transactions. Tap the arrows to move forward or backward one day at a time

heading: Daily Total Display
text: When the day has transactions (or in selection mode), below the date you'll see: A positive total (with + prefix) when income exceeds expenses A negative total when expenses exceed income The total updates in real-time as you navigate between days In selection mode, the total shows the sum of only the selected transactions (for an account, the net impact on that account)

heading: Calendar View
text: The calendar is shown at the top of the page when you open this screen. It and the selected day’s transactions scroll together: swipe up to move past the calendar and read more transactions, or scroll back to the top to choose another date. Tapping the date or its calendar icon in the fixed header also returns to the calendar. There is no calendar hide/show toggle.

heading: Month Navigation
text: At the top of the calendar: Left Arrow (<) - Go to the previous month Month and Year - Tap to open a month/year picker for faster navigation Right Arrow (>) - Go to the next month

heading: Calendar Grid
text: A row of weekday labels (e.g. Mon, Tue, …) appears above the grid. The calendar displays only the current month’s days with the following features: Day Tiles: Each day shows the day number Days with transactions display daily income (in the income color with + prefix) and expenses (in red with - prefix) The selected day is highlighted with a colored border and subtle background Today's date has a special border highlight Future days appear slightly faded Empty cells before the first day of the month are left blank (other months’ days are not shown) Actions: Tap any day in the current month to select it and view its transactions Selecting a day updates the header, daily total, and transactions below without closing the calendar or automatically scrolling away from it. It exits selection mode and clears any selected transactions.

heading: Month/Year Picker
text: When you tap the month name in the calendar header, a picker opens allowing you to: Quickly jump to any month Navigate between years See which months have transaction data

heading: Transaction List
text: Below the calendar, you'll see all transactions for the selected day.

heading: Transaction Display
text: Each transaction shows: Category icon - Visual indicator of the transaction category Category name - The budget category this transaction belongs to Amount - The transaction amount with appropriate color coding: Green with + prefix for income Category section color for expenses

heading: Additional Details
text: Transactions may also display: Receipt icon - Shown after the category name, or after the description when that is the row title, when the transaction belongs to a receipt and is listed on its own. Grouping follows the list you opened this day from: account and set days can still fold several receipt items into one group, and that group shows the receipt icon after the category name when every item uses the same category. Recurring icon (↻) - Indicates a recurring transaction Confirmation icon (?) - Indicates confirmation is required Transfer icon (↔) - Indicates a transfer between accounts Contact badge - Shows associated person or business Account badge - Shows which account was used Description - Any notes added to the transaction Tags - Hashtags for additional categorization

heading: Grouped Transactions
text: Depending on context, transactions may be grouped by: Receipt - Multiple items from the same receipt shown together Contact - Transactions with the same person or business grouped

heading: Empty State
text: If there are no transactions for the selected day: A receipt icon is displayed A “No results found” message is shown

heading: Selection Mode
text: The Day Transactions Screen includes a powerful selection mode for analyzing multiple transactions at once.

heading: Activating Selection Mode
text: Tap the checkmark icon in the top-right corner of the header to enter selection mode.

heading: Using Selection Mode
text: When in selection mode: Tap individual transactions to select or deselect them Tap a group header to select or deselect all transactions in that group Selected transactions show a checkmark indicator The header total updates to show the combined total of only selected transactions

heading: Viewing Selected Totals
text: While in selection mode, the daily total in the header changes to show: The combined amount of all selected transactions This helps you quickly calculate subtotals for specific purchases or activities

heading: Exiting Selection Mode
text: Tap the checkmark icon again to exit selection mode and clear all selections. Note: Selection mode is not available for future dates (dates that haven't occurred yet).

heading: Tapping Transactions
text: Different transaction types have different behaviors when tapped: Regular Transactions (Income/Expenses): Opens the Edit Transaction screen where you can modify all details. Recurring Preview Transactions: For transactions that are previews of upcoming recurring entries, tapping opens options to: View the recurring template Confirm the transaction early Skip this occurrence Confirmation-Required Transactions: For scheduled transactions requiring your approval, tapping opens a confirmation dialog with options to: Confirm the transaction Skip this occurrence Edit before confirming Transfers: Opens the Edit Transfer screen to modify transfer details. Balance Adjustments: Opens the Edit Balance screen to modify the adjustment. Long-press a transaction (except previews and confirmation-required ones) for edit, duplicate, and delete. If it belongs to a receipt, Edit receipt opens that receipt with all of its items.

heading: Adding New Transactions
text: The floating action button(s) at the bottom of the screen let you quickly add new entries. The available options depend on the context you're viewing:

heading: Global View (All Transactions)
text: A single Add Transaction button opens the Add Transaction screen with the selected date pre-filled. To create a receipt from there, use expense mode and tap the split icon next to the Category field.

heading: Account View
text: A single + button opens a menu with options to: Add Transaction - Record a new expense or income for this account (available for foreign-currency accounts as well as main-currency accounts) Add Receipt - Add or enter a receipt for this account (only for accounts in your main currency; hidden for foreign-currency accounts) Transfer Between Accounts - Create a transfer involving this account Balance Increase - Add a positive balance adjustment Balance Decrease - Add a negative balance adjustment

heading: Category View
text: A single + button opens the Add Transaction screen with: The selected category pre-filled The selected date pre-filled

heading: Context Awareness
text: The Day Transactions Screen adapts based on where you access it from:

heading: From the Main Transactions Screen
text: Shows all transactions across all accounts and categories Both floating action buttons (receipt and add) are available

heading: From an Account
text: Shows only transactions for that specific account Account-specific add options are available Account badges may be hidden since you're already viewing one account

heading: From a Category
text: Shows only transactions for that specific category Add transaction opens with the category pre-selected

heading: From a Contact, Tag, or Section
text: Shows only transactions related to that entity No floating action button is shown; you cannot add transactions from this screen when viewing by contact, tag, or section

heading: Day Tile Colors
text: In the calendar grid: Income color - Income totals for that day (typically green; follows budget section color) Red amounts - Expense totals for that day Highlighted border - Currently selected day or today Faded appearance - Future dates

heading: Transaction Colors
text: In the transaction list: Income color with + - Income transactions (typically green; follows budget section) Section color - Expense transactions (matches budget section) Faded appearance - Preview/scheduled transactions not yet confirmed

heading: Tips for Using the Day Transactions Screen
text: Quick date navigation - Use the left/right arrows to quickly check adjacent days Use the calendar for jumping - Tap the date in the header to return to the calendar, then choose any day, especially when looking at historical data Check daily patterns - The calendar's income/expense indicators help you spot spending patterns at a glance Selection mode for subtotals - Use selection mode to quickly calculate the total for specific purchases or categories Future planning - View future dates to see upcoming scheduled and recurring transactions Add transactions on the right date - When viewing a specific date, new transactions automatically use that date Month picker for long jumps - Tap the month name to quickly jump to months far in the past

heading: Navigating Back
text: Tap the X (close) button in the top-left corner to exit the Day Transactions Screen and return to the previous screen.

The Accounts Screen is where you manage all your financial accounts. You can organize your bank accounts, cash, credit cards, investments, and any other accounts you use to manage money. Accounts are organized into groups to help you keep things tidy and see your total balances at a glance.

heading: Accessing the Accounts Screen
text: You can access the Accounts Screen by: Tapping the "Accounts" tab in the bottom navigation

heading: Understanding Account Groups
text: Account groups help you organize related accounts together. For example, you might have: Main Accounts - Your primary checking account, savings, and cash Credit Cards - All your credit cards in one place Investments - Brokerage accounts, retirement funds Savings Goals - Separate accounts for vacation, emergency fund, etc. Debts - Loans, mortgages, money you owe Each group displays its own icon and shows the combined total balance of all accounts within it (when all accounts share the same currency).

heading: Account Groups
text: The main area displays your account groups as expandable cards. Each group card shows: Group icon (on the left) - A visual identifier for the group type Group name - The name you gave the group (e.g., "Main Accounts", "Savings") Total balance (on the right) - The combined balance of all accounts in the group Only shown when all accounts in the group use the same currency Positive balances appear in the app's primary color Negative balances appear in red Menu button (three dots) - Opens group actions

heading: Expanding and Collapsing Groups
text: Tap the group header to expand or collapse it When expanded, you'll see all accounts within that group When a group has no accounts, an Add account button appears inside the group card for quick access The app remembers which groups you had expanded, so they stay that way when you return

heading: Individual Accounts
text: Within each expanded group, accounts are listed showing: Account name - The name you gave the account (e.g., "Chase Checking", "Cash Wallet") Default indicator (star icon) - Shows if this is your default account Description - Any notes you added about the account Balance - Current account balance with currency symbol Positive balances appear in the primary color Negative balances appear in red Goal progress - If the account has a goal, the row shows current balance vs target balance, remaining or over-goal amount, remaining percentage, and a progress bar Menu button (three dots) - Opens account actions

heading: Quick Action Buttons
text: At the bottom of the screen, you'll find floating action buttons for common tasks:

heading: When You Have One or More Accounts
text: Decrease Balance (minus icon) - Quickly record a balance decrease on any account Increase Balance (plus icon) - Quickly record a balance increase on any account

heading: When You Have Two or More Accounts
text: Transfer (swap arrows icon) - Move money between your accounts These buttons provide fast access to the most common account operations without needing to open the menu.

heading: Top Bar Actions
text: When at least one active account exists, the top bar shows: Match bank statement (upload icon) - Opens Statement Import. Free users see a gold Pro badge on the icon; tapping it opens the Pro upgrade page instead of import. Pro users go straight to Statement Import (choose the account there if it is not already selected) → Bank statement matching More menu (menu icon) - Opens the options listed below

heading: Top Bar Menu
text: Tap the menu icon in the top right corner to access additional options:

heading: Add Group
text: Create a new account group to organize your accounts. Groups can have custom names and icons.

heading: Add Account
text: Create a new account. You'll need to: Select which group it belongs to Enter a name for the account Set the starting balance Choose the currency Optionally add a description Optionally set it as your default account Optionally set a balance goal for the account

heading: Transfer Between Accounts
text: Move money from one account to another. This is useful for: Recording bank transfers Moving money between checking and savings Tracking credit card payments Recording any money movement between your accounts

heading: Increase Balance
text: Add money to an account without creating a regular income transaction. Use this for: Corrections when your balance doesn't match your bank Initial deposits when setting up a new account Any balance adjustment that shouldn't appear as regular income

heading: Decrease Balance
text: Remove money from an account without creating a regular expense transaction. Use this for: Corrections when your balance doesn't match your bank Fees or charges that don't fit a budget category Any balance adjustment that shouldn't appear as regular expenses

heading: Match bank statement
text: Import a CSV or XLSX bank statement and reconcile rows with existing transactions (same destination as the top-bar upload icon). Free users see a Pro badge on this row and are sent to the Pro upgrade page; Pro users open Statement Import → Bank statement matching

heading: Change Order
text: Rearrange the order of your account groups and accounts within groups. Drag items to reorder them however you prefer.

heading: Archive
text: View and manage your archived accounts and groups. Archiving lets you hide accounts you no longer use while keeping their history.

heading: Tapping an Account
text: Tap any account to view all transactions for that account. This opens a filtered transaction list showing: All income and expenses involving this account Transfers to and from this account Balance adjustments The account's transaction history over time

heading: Long-Pressing an Account (or Tapping the Menu Button)
text: Opens a menu with these options: Increase Balance - Add money to this specific account Decrease Balance - Remove money from this specific account Match bank statement - Import a CSV or XLSX bank statement for this account and reconcile statement rows with existing transactions (Pro; free users see a Pro badge and are sent to upgrade) → Bank statement matching Flow Chart - Open an account-specific flow screen with inflow, outflow, and balance trends for that account across the selected period Analytics - Open the general Analytics screen filtered to this account for breakdowns by category, contact, tag, description, and more Edit - Change the account's name, description, currency, balance, group, default status, or goal Archive - Hide the account from the main list (keeps all history) Delete - Permanently remove the account (only available if the account has no transactions) Note: You cannot delete an account that has transactions. Archive it instead to hide it while preserving your financial history.

heading: Account Flow Chart
text: The account flow chart is a dedicated screen for understanding how money moves through one account over time.

heading: What It Shows
text: Period picker in the top bar - Change the date range for this account Summary card - Total inflow and outflow for the selected period Flow type filters - Switch between All, Inflow, Outflow, and Balance Trend chart - View the account's movement grouped by days, weeks, months, or years depending on the selected range Unlike the general Analytics screen, this account flow view is focused on money moving in and out of the selected account itself.

heading: Account Goals
text: Account goals let you track progress toward a target balance on a specific account. They are useful for savings targets such as an emergency fund or vacation fund, and can also represent a balance you want to reach when paying down an account.

heading: Setting a Goal
text: When creating or editing an account, tap Set goal to show the goal fields: Target balance - The balance you want this account to reach Goal start - The balance where progress starts; this defaults to the account's current balance when you enable the goal If you set a target balance and leave Goal start empty, Budgetum uses the account balance as the starting point for goal progress.

heading: How Goals Are Displayed
text: Accounts with goals show extra progress information directly in the account list: Current balance compared with the target balance Amount remaining until the target, or the amount over the target after passing it Remaining or over-goal percentage A small progress bar Progress is calculated from the Goal start balance to the Target balance. If the target is higher than the start, progress increases as the balance grows. If the target is lower than the start, progress increases as the balance goes down toward the target.

heading: Editing or Removing a Goal
text: Open the account menu and choose Edit to change goal values. Clearing the target balance removes the goal from the account.

heading: Account Group Actions
text: Long-press a group header (or tap the menu button) to see group options: Add Account - Create a new account within this group Edit - Change the group's name or icon Archive - Hide the entire group (and all its accounts) from the main list Delete - Permanently remove the group (only available if the group has no accounts)

heading: Creating a New Account
text: When adding a new account, you'll fill in:

heading: Required Fields
text: Group - Which group this account belongs to Name - A unique name for the account (e.g., "Main Checking", "Vacation Savings"). Duplicate names are not allowed. Starting Balance - The current balance in this account

heading: Optional Fields
text: Currency - Defaults to your app's primary currency, but can be different for foreign accounts. Foreign-currency accounts can be used for normal income and expense transactions (with a separate budget amount), for multi-currency transfers, and for balance tracking. Receipts and the default-account option stay limited to the primary currency. Description - Notes about the account (e.g., "Emergency fund - don't touch!") Set as Default - Make this your default account for new transactions (only available for accounts using your primary currency) Goal - Optional target balance and starting balance used to show progress in the account list

heading: Transfers Between Accounts
text: When transferring money, you'll specify: From Account - The account sending money To Account - The account receiving money From Amount - How much is leaving the source account To Amount - How much is arriving in the destination account (automatically matches the from amount, but you can change it for currency conversions or fee adjustments) Date - When the transfer happened Description - Optional notes about the transfer Make Recurring - Set up automatic repeating transfers Multi-Currency Transfers: If you're transferring between accounts with different currencies, you can enter different amounts for "from" and "to" to account for exchange rates. The amount picker may offer an optional market-rate quick suggestion between the two currencies. When both amounts are filled, the form can also show a muted implied rate helper under the amount fields (destination ÷ source from the numbers you entered)—this is not a live market quote. Scheduled Transfers: If you set a future date, you can optionally mark the transfer as requiring confirmation before it affects your balances.

heading: Balance Adjustments
text: Balance adjustments let you correct your account balance without creating regular transactions. This is useful when: Your tracked balance doesn't match your actual bank balance You find discrepancies during reconciliation You need to account for fees that don't fit a category You receive or lose money outside your normal transactions

heading: Increase Balance
text: Adds money to an account. Records when and why the balance increased.

heading: Decrease Balance
text: Removes money from an account. Records when and why the balance decreased. Both adjustment types support: Setting a specific date Adding a description Making it recurring (for regular adjustments like monthly bank fees) Requiring confirmation for future-dated adjustments

heading: Archive
text: The Archive stores accounts and groups you've hidden from your main view. Archiving is perfect for: Old bank accounts you've closed Credit cards you've paid off Temporary accounts you no longer use Keeping your main list clean and focused

heading: Viewing the Archive
text: Access the archive from the top bar menu. Here you'll see all archived groups and accounts.

heading: Archive Actions
text: For archived groups : Restore - Bring the group back to your main list Delete - Permanently remove (only if the group has no accounts) For archived accounts : View Transactions - See the account's transaction history Restore - Bring the account back to its group Delete - Permanently remove (only if the account has no transactions)

heading: Reordering Accounts and Groups
text: From "Change Order" in the menu, you can customize how your accounts appear:

heading: Reordering Groups
text: Drag and drop groups to arrange them in your preferred order. The first group appears at the top of your Accounts screen.

heading: Reordering Accounts Within a Group
text: Tap a group to open the account order view for that group, then drag and drop to reorder its accounts. This affects the display order within that group.

heading: Getting Started Help
text: When you first open the Accounts screen (or have no account groups), you'll see a helpful guide explaining: How account groups work Suggested group structures Examples of common setups You can dismiss this guide once you're comfortable with the concept. The guide provides examples like: Main Accounts - Checking, Savings, Cash Debts - Credit Cards, Loans, Mortgages Investments - Stocks, Retirement, Crypto Savings Goals - Emergency Fund, Vacation, Car Other - Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards

heading: Tips for Using Accounts
text: Use groups strategically - Organize accounts by purpose (spending, saving, debt) rather than by institution Set a default account - Your most-used account should be the default, so it's pre-selected when adding transactions Keep balances accurate - Regularly compare your app balances to your actual accounts and use balance adjustments to fix any differences Use descriptions - Add notes to accounts to remember their purpose or any special rules Use transfers for internal movement - When you move money between your own accounts, use Transfer rather than creating separate income/expense transactions Consider negative balances - Credit cards and loans typically have negative balances, which is normal and expected

The Statement Import screen helps you reconcile one account in Budgetum with a bank statement file. You import a CSV or XLSX file, tell Budgetum which columns contain the date, amount, and description, and then compare the imported statement rows with transactions that already exist in that account. This feature is designed to speed up account reconciliation. It does not replace your full transaction history automatically. Instead, it helps you match, create, or ignore rows one by one or in batches.

heading: Accessing Statement Import
text: You can open Statement Import from the Accounts screen in several ways: Top-bar upload icon ( Match bank statement ) — opens Statement Import; pick the account on the import screen if needed Accounts More menu — same Match bank statement action Account row more menu (or long-press the account row) — Match bank statement for that account (account is pre-selected) Free users see a gold Pro badge on these entry points and are sent to the Pro upgrade page instead of import. Availability: Available only in Budgetum Pro Each import belongs to a single account The English action label is Match bank statement (no Beta suffix on that action string)

heading: What Statement Import Does
text: Statement Import compares: Imported statement rows from your bank file Existing account transactions already recorded in Budgetum It helps you identify: Rows that already match existing transactions Existing transactions that appear in Budgetum but were not matched to the imported statement Statement rows that still need action This works for: Regular income and expense transactions Transfers Balance increases and decreases Receipt groups, when several receipt items together equal one statement amount

heading: Help Card
text: Before or while setting up an import (account + file + column mapping), a dismissible help card can appear with short steps and matching tips (auto-matched rows, unmatched ? rows, and that starting a new import only clears statement rows for that account). Title: Match your bank statement Dismiss with Got it! Dismissal is remembered; More → Tips & Assistance → Reset Tutorial restores it along with other tutorial hints

heading: Supported Files
text: You can import: CSV XLSX For best results: The file should contain a clear header row The header row should be placed directly above the transaction data The data should include at least a date, a description, and an amount representation If Budgetum cannot detect the header row automatically, you can often fix it with Import options (the more menu on the Match columns card) instead of choosing another file: Select header row — pick which row in the file contains column titles (Date, Amount, Description, etc.). Budgetum re-reads the grid from that row. Date format — choose how ambiguous numeric dates (for example 03/04/2026 ) should be interpreted: automatic from your device locale, day/month/year, month/day/year, or year/month/day. If the file cannot be read at all, choose a different file or export format.

heading: Import Setup
text: Before saving the import, you configure how the source file maps into Budgetum.

heading: 1. Select a file
text: Tap the Statement file field and choose a CSV or XLSX file from your device. While Budgetum processes the file, it shows status messages such as: Reading the selected file Analyzing the file structure Auto-matching columns Validating rows

heading: 2. Match columns
text: Use the more menu (three dots) on the Match columns card when you need Select header row or Date format (optional). After the file is read, Budgetum asks you to match source columns to required fields: Date column Description column Amount column , or separate Credit and Debit columns Each required field must use a different source column.

heading: 3. Choose an amount mode
text: You can import statement amounts in three ways:

heading: Signed amount (+/-)
text: Use this when one amount column already includes positive and negative values Positive values are treated as money entering the account Negative values are treated as money leaving the account

heading: Not signed (expense by default)
text: Use this when the statement has a single amount column without signs Imported rows are treated as expenses by default

heading: Credit and debit columns
text: Use this when the bank exports money in and money out into separate columns Budgetum calculates one signed amount from those two fields

heading: 4. Review the preview
text: Budgetum shows a preview of the first imported rows using the selected columns so you can confirm the mapping before saving.

heading: 5. Save the import
text: When validation succeeds, tap the check button in the top bar. Saving the import: Stores the parsed rows for that account Remembers your column names for future auto-matching Starts the reconciliation view Builds matching rules from exact matches for future suggestions

heading: Validation Rules
text: Budgetum checks the file before it saves anything. Common validation requirements: The file must contain rows The required mapped columns must exist The date and description must be matched The amount mapping must match the selected amount mode Required fields must use different columns Each row must contain a valid date Each row must contain a valid amount If any row fails validation, Budgetum shows the row number and stops the save so you can correct the mapping or choose another file.

heading: Reconciliation View
text: After saving, the screen changes from setup mode to a date-grouped reconciliation list. Rows are grouped by date and may appear in three states:

heading: Matched rows
text: These statement rows were matched to one or more existing transactions in the selected account. How automatic matching works: Budgetum builds match candidates from the account’s transactions in the imported date range: Each normal transaction is one candidate (amount is the signed movement for this account) Receipt lines that share a receipt ID are combined into one receipt-group candidate whose amount is the sum of those lines A statement row auto-matches only when there is exactly one remaining candidate with the same date and the same signed amount (compared to the cent) If several transactions share the same date and amount, Budgetum does not guess. The row stays unmatched until you choose manually Each candidate can be used by only one statement row Receipt groups can therefore match a single bank charge that equals the total of several receipt items. Matched entries appear slightly faded to show they are already reconciled. Opening a matched transaction can offer Unlink from statement to clear that link.

heading: Existing-only rows
text: These are transactions that already exist in Budgetum for that account and date range but were not paired with any imported row. This helps you notice: Transactions entered in Budgetum but not present in the statement Duplicate or extra records Timing differences between your app and the bank

heading: Unmatched rows
text: These are statement rows that still need your decision. Unmatched rows may show suggestion badges for: Category Contact Transfer to/from an account Those suggestions come from learned matching rules based on previous exact matches (see below). The badges may highlight the most-used pattern. When approving a row with multiple compatible category/contact or transfer variants, you always choose a variant before anything is created.

heading: Row Actions
text: Tap an unmatched row to open actions.

heading: Approve
text: Approve creates one transaction using the statement date and amount, the current account, and a learned category/contact or transfer variant. A transfer variant shows Transfer to {account} for outgoing amounts or Transfer from {account} for incoming amounts. It creates a transfer between the current account and the remembered account, using the statement amount for both sides and leaving the transfer description empty. Both accounts must be active and use the same currency. Approve is disabled if no compatible category or transfer suggestion exists; use Create transaction or Transfer to choose fields yourself. Different-currency transfers still use the Transfer form so you can enter both amounts. With one compatible variant, creation starts immediately. With multiple variants, Select variant opens first. Variants are sorted by usage, most-used first; ties use the most recent usage. No counts are shown beside variants. Selecting one creates the transaction; dismissing the picker creates nothing.

heading: Approve all (N)
text: In an unmatched row's actions, Approve all (N) appears when more than one unmatched row in the same account's current import shares the same cleaned description and can use at least one of the selected row's compatible variants. The group includes rows hidden by search and spans all dates in the import. Each transaction keeps its own date and amount. The variant choice works like Approve , and the selected category/contact or transfer account applies to compatible rows in the group: An expense category accepts outgoing expenses and incoming refunds.
