An income category accepts incoming amounts only. Outgoing rows stay unmatched. A transfer variant accepts only its remembered direction: outgoing to that account or incoming from it. Rows in the opposite direction stay unmatched. Zero amounts are not approved. N is the eligible group size before choosing a variant. The number created can be smaller when the chosen variant excludes rows with an incompatible direction. A completion message reports how many transactions were created. Already matched rows are excluded, and further approval actions are unavailable while approval is in progress. Transfer approval checks current matches again, so a transfer already created from the other account’s statement can match instead of being created twice. Matching still requires the same date and account amount. If several existing transfers could fit, use Select existing to resolve the ambiguity; approval leaves those rows unmatched.

heading: Create transaction
text: Creates a normal income or expense transaction from the statement row. Budgetum pre-fills: The selected account The statement date The absolute amount Suggested category and contact, if available

heading: Transfer
text: Creates a transfer between accounts using the statement row. Budgetum pre-fills: The statement date The amount The selected account as the source or destination, depending on whether the row is outgoing or incoming

heading: Increase balance
text: Creates a balance increase linked to the imported row.

heading: Decrease balance
text: Creates a balance decrease linked to the imported row.

heading: Select existing
text: Opens Select transactions so you can manually link the statement row to existing Budgetum activity on the same date . You can select: One transaction whose amount already equals the statement amount, or Several same-day candidates (including receipt groups) whose amounts add up exactly to the statement amount The screen shows: Remaining amount still needed Selected of target totals A check action that stays disabled until the selected total matches the statement amount exactly This is useful when: More than one possible transaction exists for the same date and amount (auto-match stayed unmatched on purpose) One bank charge covers several Budgetum transactions You already recorded the activity and just want to confirm the link Manual links are remembered by a row fingerprint (account, date, amount, cleaned description) and the selected transaction IDs. If you clear the import and re-import the same statement later, Budgetum can restore those links automatically when the matching transactions are still available.

heading: Ignore
text: Removes the imported row from the saved import without deleting any real transaction. Use this when the statement row should not be tracked in Budgetum.

heading: Bulk Actions And Learned Suggestions
text: Statement Import can learn from successful exact matches. When Budgetum finds a reliable exact match, it can remember: A cleaned version of the statement description (noisy prefixes, dates, times, and short reference codes are reduced so similar merchant text still matches) The category used The contact used For a transfer, the other account and direction, stored separately for incoming and outgoing rows How often that pattern was used Transfer patterns are learned both when you create a transfer using a statement row’s Transfer action and when that row is matched to one existing transfer, automatically or through Select existing . The date and amount must match the row. Only transfers between accounts with the same currency and equal amounts on both sides teach quick-approval patterns; a grouped match to several transactions does not. Transfer suggestions are hidden if either account is archived, the other account is deleted, or the accounts no longer use the same currency. Learning is specific to the imported account and statement description. Incoming and outgoing transfer patterns remain separate even when their descriptions are identical; the amount’s sign determines direction, without removing “from” or “to” from the description. Later, unmatched rows with a similar cleaned description can show suggested badges. Use Approve for one row or Approve all (N) in that row's actions for repeated descriptions. When multiple compatible patterns exist, choose one in Select variant , ordered by usage and then recency. There is no global action to create transactions across unrelated descriptions.

heading: Search And Visibility Options
text: After an import is saved, the top bar offers extra tools:

heading: Search
text: Search helps filter the reconciliation list by terms such as: Description text Date Amount Suggested category Suggested contact Suggested transfer account and direction

heading: Show or hide matched rows
text: You can hide already matched transactions to focus only on what still needs attention. Use the eye icon in the top bar ( Hide matched transactions / Show matched transactions ). When matched rows are hidden and nothing else is left (no unmatched statement rows and no existing-only transactions), the screen shows a check mark with All rows are matched : the account is fully reconciled for this import. Tap the eye icon again to see the matched rows.

heading: Start New Import
text: From the more menu, you can choose Start new import . This action: Clears the saved imported statement rows for that account Keeps your real Budgetum transactions Keeps learned column matches Lets you import a fresh file for the same account Use this when you selected the wrong file, need a newer statement, or want to restart reconciliation from scratch.

heading: Important Notes
text: Statement Import is account-specific Matching compares statement rows only against transactions in that account and within the imported date range Auto-match requires a unique same-date, same-amount candidate; duplicates stay unmatched until you use Select existing You can match one statement row to multiple same-day transactions when their amounts sum to the statement amount Manual matches can persist across clearing and re-importing the same statement file for that account Budgetum does not delete existing transactions when you restart or clear an import Ignoring a row removes only the imported statement row, not any transaction Manual or auto-linked rows can later be opened in their normal edit screens, where you can unlink them from the statement

heading: Tips For Best Results
text: Use statement files with a clear header row directly above the data. Start with accounts you reconcile often, such as your main checking account or card. If possible, import a larger date range instead of a very short statement. More rows give Budgetum more chances to auto-match existing transactions and learn useful category/contact suggestions. If your file uses separate money-in and money-out columns, choose Credit and debit columns . Hide matched rows after the first pass to focus on what still needs action. When several Budgetum transactions share one bank charge, use Select existing and multi-select until Remaining reaches zero. If same-day duplicates block auto-match, that is intentional—use Select existing to pick the correct one. Let the feature learn over time. Repeated exact matches improve future suggestions for categories and contacts. When Select variant opens after Approve or Approve all, pick the category/contact or transfer pattern that fits the statement description. Incoming refunds can use an expense category.

The Analytics screen provides visual charts and detailed breakdowns of your spending and income patterns. It helps you understand where your money goes, identify trends over time, and make informed financial decisions.

heading: Accessing Analytics
text: You can open Analytics from: The Analytics action on the Budget screen The "Analytics" option in a category's menu on the Budget screen The "Analytics" option in a section's menu on the Budget screen The pie chart icon when viewing an account, contact, or tag's transactions The Analytics action in a saved set’s menu For accounts, there is also a separate Flow Chart screen available from the account menu on the Accounts screen. That view is different from Analytics: it focuses on account inflow, outflow, and balance trends for one account rather than category/contact/tag-style breakdowns. Analytics can be viewed for: Your entire budget (all transactions) A specific account A specific budget section A specific category A specific contact A specific tag A specific expense type (Needs, Wants, or Savings) A contact type (such as Stores) A saved set, including its include/exclude conditions

heading: Title Bar
text: The top bar shows: Back button - Return to the previous screen Title - The current entity (e.g., "Groceries" or "Store A"). View toggle - Switch between Breakdown view (pie chart icon) and Trends view (bar chart icon) More analytics (⋮) - Opens extra analytics views. Currently includes Spending calendar (full-year daily spending heatmap)

heading: Breadcrumbs
text: After drilling down, a compact, horizontally scrollable text path appears below the summary in both Breakdown and Trends, for example Vacation › Groceries › Store A . The app-bar title still shows the current entity. Tap an earlier breadcrumb to return to that screen with its period and selected view restored; Back returns one level. When the selection has no data, the path remains available above the empty state.

heading: Period Picker
text: Below the title bar, the period picker lets you select the date range for analysis: Compare icon (⇄, left side of the period picker) - Opens Compare period options so you can compare the current range with a previous period or the same period last year (see Period comparison below). The icon is brighter when comparison is active. Left/Right arrows - Navigate between periods (month, year, etc.) Start date - Tap to open the date picker and set a custom start date; the date picker offers quick options such as "This month" and "This year" (select full month or full year). End date - Tap to open the date picker and set a custom end date Dropdown (down arrow) - Opens a list of quick period options: This month, This quarter, This half-year, This year, Previous year, All time

heading: Period comparison
text: Period comparison lets you judge whether income and spending are up or down versus another date range. It applies to the summary card , breakdown list , and trends details while comparison is enabled.

heading: How to enable it
text: Tap the compare arrows icon on the left of the period picker Choose one option in the bottom sheet: Previous period - The equally long range immediately before your current start–end dates. For whole-month selections (for example one month, one quarter, or a half-year of full months), Budgetum shifts by that many calendar months. For other custom ranges, it shifts by the same number of days. Same period last year - The same start and end dates shifted back one year (day is clamped to the last valid day of the month when needed, for example Feb 29 → Feb 28) To turn it off, open the sheet again and tap Disable comparison The sheet shows the resolved comparison date range under each option so you can confirm what will be used.

heading: What changes when comparison is on
text: Summary card - Income and expense totals show change indicators versus the compared period Breakdown list - Each row can show amount and percentage change versus the same item in the compared period (higher spending is treated as worse for expenses; higher income is better for income) Trends - Selected-period details can include comparison deltas when comparison data is available Period comparison is separate from the Trends vs Income overlay (which compares expenses to income inside the same selected period).

heading: Summary Card
text: At the top of the content area, a Summary Card shows: Income - Total money received in the period Expenses - Total money spent in the period Remaining - The difference (income minus expenses); shown in Trends view only when you have income, and not shown in Breakdown view When period comparison is enabled, income and expense lines also show how they changed versus the compared period. The summary covers the full selected period and every active filter, regardless of how many transaction rows are currently displayed. It shows gross expenses and received income, including refunds (offset income). For a $100 purchase and a $20 refund, the summary shows $100 expenses and $20 income; the expense breakdown shows $80 net spending. See Refunds and tag allocation .

heading: Breakdown View (Pie Chart)
text: The Breakdown view shows how your spending or income is distributed across different categories, contacts, or other groupings.

heading: Income/Expense Dropdown
text: When you have both income and expenses, a dropdown (top right in the filter area) lets you switch between: Expenses - See how your spending is distributed Income - See how your income is distributed

heading: Breakdown Type
text: Below the income/expense dropdown, filter buttons let you choose what to break down by. Available breakdowns depend on what you're viewing: Starting context Possible breakdowns Budget (all) Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts Account Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Descriptions Section Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Category Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Contact Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Contact type Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Tag Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Accounts, Descriptions Expense type Sections, Categories, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Saved set Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions Only breakdowns that separate the current transactions into at least two different nonempty groups appear. Single-group breakdowns and tags attached to exactly the same purchases are omitted. A grouping already selected in the navigation path is not offered again. Equal amounts do not make a grouping redundant: two stores with $50 each still represent different purchases. Groups may overlap. If both tags occur on every matching transaction, Tags adds no split and is hidden. A single populated group plus transactions without that value is also hidden; no extra “Unassigned” group is created.

heading: Transactions option
text: Transactions is the last option in the existing, left-aligned selector. It uses the standard dense transaction rows, grouped by date and then by receipt/contact where possible. Expenses includes matching refunds; Income excludes refunds. Tap a group to inspect its matching transactions, or use the usual transaction edit and long-press actions. The percentage control is hidden while Transactions is selected. When no useful breakdown remains, transactions appear automatically and the redundant selector is hidden. Initially about 100 transactions are displayed. A receipt/contact group crossing the cutoff is included in full, so a page can exceed 100. Show more extends the list by another approximately 100 transactions without splitting groups. Groups contain only transactions matching the active analytics filters, even if the original receipt contains other purchases. The display limit does not affect totals, percentages, comparisons, or charts. Changing periods reevaluates the available breakdowns. An explicitly selected Transactions view stays selected.

heading: Percentage Mode (Expenses Only)
text: When viewing an expense breakdown and the period has income, a percentage control lets you choose how percentages are calculated: % of Expenses - Each item’s share of the positive net expense totals in the breakdown. Rows with zero or negative net spending show 0%. % of Period Income - Each item as a percentage of your total income for the period % of Entity Income - Each item as a percentage of income for this specific entity (shown only when viewing an account, contact, tag, etc. that has income and where that entity's income differs from total period income) This helps you understand spending relative to what you earned.

heading: Breakdown List
text: The main area shows a list of items with: For each item: Icon and name - The category, section, contact, or tag Amount - Total spent or received. When viewing expenses, if the item has offset income (matched income), a small “+X” shows the offset amount and the main amount is net (expense minus offset). Percentage - Share of the total Progress bar - Visual representation of the proportion Period comparison deltas (when enabled) - Amount and/or percentage change versus the compared period Items are sorted by net amount (largest first). Tapping an item adds it to the current analytics selection and opens the next level for the same period and income/expense mode. Earlier selections remain active, including saved-set conditions: Vacation → Groceries → Store A shows only grocery purchases at that store within Vacation. Descriptions open matching transactions directly. Changing dates or comparing periods keeps every selection in your analytics path. For example, changing months while viewing Vacation › Groceries › Store A shows that month’s grocery purchases at Store A within Vacation. It does not switch to all Store A purchases. Returning through breadcrumbs restores the earlier screen’s period and selection. Analytics refreshes after transaction changes and after closing a transaction group.

heading: Trends View (Bar Chart)
text: The Trends view shows how your spending or income changes over time, helping you spot patterns and trends.

heading: Display Type
text: Toggle buttons let you choose what to display: Available display types: All Expenses - Total expenses over time Needs+Wants - All expenses excluding savings (when you have both savings and other expenses) Needs - Only essential expense categories (when you have them) Wants - Only discretionary expense categories (when you have them) Savings - Only savings categories (when you have them) Income - Total income over time Remaining - Balance (income minus expenses) over time (when you have both income and expenses) Saved + remaining - Running total of savings plus remaining money (when you have income, expenses, and savings) Only types that have data appear as options.

heading: Time Period
text: The chart groups data into time buckets (one bar per day, week, month, or year). You choose the grouping via a period selector; only periods that make sense for your date range are offered: Days - One bar per day. Available only when the selected range is about 2 months or less (62 days or fewer). Weeks - One bar per week. Available when the range is about 4 months or less (124 days or fewer). Months - One bar per month. Available when the range is less than about 3 years. Years - One bar per year. Always available, regardless of date range. For example, "This month" will typically offer Days and Weeks; "This year" will offer Weeks, Months, and Years; "All time" might offer only Months and Years. Tap the period selector (showing the current grouping) to switch.

heading: Income Comparison (vs Income)
text: When viewing expense data and you have income: A toggle appears: vs Income Enable it to overlay your income on the expense chart This helps visualize if you're spending more or less than you earn in the same selected period This is different from period comparison (previous period / same period last year) controlled from the period picker.

heading: Section colors on expense bars
text: When the Trends display type is an expense view (All expenses, Needs+Wants, Needs, Wants, or Savings) and section breakdown data is available, a Sections toggle (pie-chart outline icon) appears next to vs Income . Turn it on to paint each expense bar as a stack of section colors (each section uses that section’s color from your budget) Sections are stacked with the largest overall share toward the bottom for a stable order across periods Very small section slices (under about 1% of the bar) are omitted from the stack so the chart stays readable Dimmed (non-selected) bars keep the same section colors at lower opacity Selecting a period can show the matching section breakdown details using those same section colors Turn the toggle off to return to solid expense bars (theme expense/error color, or income color when the display type is Savings).

heading: Chart Display
text: The bar chart shows: Axes: X-axis (bottom) — Time periods (days, weeks, months, or years); only a subset of labels is shown to keep the chart readable. Y-axis (left) — Amount in your currency. Bars — Height is the total for that period. The chart has light horizontal grid lines to help read values. Bar colors: Expenses (solid) — Theme error color (typically red), so they stay clearly distinct from income. When the display type is "Savings", bars use the app's income color instead. Expenses (section colors) — When the Sections toggle is on, expense bars are multi-colored stacks using each budget section’s color (see above). Income — App income color (e.g. green), used for income bars and when "vs Income" is on. Remaining (balance) — Income color for positive balance, expense (error) color for negative. Saved + remaining — Income color for positive totals, expense (error) color for negative. Grid below the chart: A grid of cells appears below the chart, one cell per time period (only periods with data are shown). Each cell shows the period label and the amount(s) for that period. The grid uses up to four columns and extends downward as needed. When period comparison is enabled, cells can also show change indicators. Selecting and scrolling: Tap a bar — Selects that period; the view scrolls so the corresponding grid cell is brought into view. Tap a grid cell — Selects that period and scrolls so the chart is visible. Tapping the same bar or cell again clears the selection. The selected bar and its grid cell are highlighted (full color and border); other bars and cells are dimmed. Use this to match a bar to its detail in the grid or to focus on one period. With Sections enabled, the selected period can show a section breakdown list that matches the stacked bar colors. Tapping a section preserves the existing analytics filters, the selected bar’s date range within the current period, and its expense-type restriction (for example, Needs).

heading: Entity-Specific Analytics
text: Analytics starts with the entity or saved set you opened it for. Every later selection adds a restriction to that starting context; it does not replace it. The following sections describe the entry views. Actual breakdown choices are limited to useful, unused groupings.

heading: Budget Analytics (All Transactions)
text: All transactions across accounts; no entity filter Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, tags, or accounts Compare income vs. expenses for the whole budget

heading: Account Analytics
text: Only transactions where this account is the source or destination of money (transfers and balance adjustments are not shown) See which categories, contacts, and tags are linked to that account’s income and expenses Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, tags, or descriptions This is different from the account-specific Flow Chart screen on the Accounts screen, which focuses on money moving through the account itself

heading: Section Analytics
text: Only transactions in categories that belong to this section (income and expenses) Break down by categories, expense types, contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions See how the section’s total is distributed and where it comes from or goes to

heading: Category Analytics
text: Only transactions in this category (income and expenses) Break down by contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions See where you spend or earn for this category and how it changes over time

heading: Contact Analytics
text: Only transactions linked to this contact (store or person) Break down by sections, categories, expense types, tags, accounts, or descriptions See what you buy or receive there and how it trends over time

heading: Tag Analytics
text: Only transactions that have this tag Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, accounts, or descriptions Useful for project or trip expense tracking

heading: Expense Type Analytics (Needs / Wants / Savings)
text: Only transactions in categories of this type (Needs, Wants, or Savings) Break down by sections, categories, contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions See how much goes to that type and where it goes

heading: Saved Set Analytics
text: Opens with the set’s resolved period and include/exclude conditions. Further selections stay inside the set: Vacation › Groceries › Store A means all three conditions apply. Changing dates reloads the set for the newly selected period; it does not edit the saved set’s definition. Saved Sets explains how to open and configure a set.

heading: What's Included
text: Analytics uses only stored transactions in the selected date range: Income and expense transactions (saved in the app) Both manual transactions and those created from receipts Transfers and balance adjustments are not loaded for analytics, so they never appear in totals or breakdowns

heading: What's Excluded
text: Analytics excludes: Preview (forecasted) transactions — recurring schedule previews for the period are not included; only saved transactions are used Transfers and balance adjustments — these are filtered out of the data set for analytics

heading: Refunds and tag allocation
text: Refunds (offset income) are included in the summary’s received-income amount and shown alongside purchases in the expense Transactions view. They are excluded from the ordinary Income breakdown. In expense breakdowns, refunds reduce each item’s gross expense to its net amount, including negative net amounts when refunds exceed purchases. If only refunds match your selection, you can still review them in Transactions. When a transaction has multiple tags, its amount is divided equally between those tags. Refunds use the same allocation: a $100 expense and $20 refund, both tagged A and B, contribute $50 expense and $10 refund to each tag, or $40 net each. Drilling into a tag shows the full matching transactions; its transaction total may therefore differ from that tag’s allocated amount in the parent breakdown. The spending calendar uses gross daily expenses or ordinary income and excludes refunds from its day shading. Its amounts therefore need not match a net expense breakdown.

heading: Date Range Matters
text: The data shown depends on your selected date range: Choose "All Time" for complete history Use the period dropdown or tap the dates for presets (This month, This year, etc.) Use custom start/end dates for specific analysis (e.g., vacation or project period)

heading: Empty State
text: If there's no data for the selected period and view: A message indicates no data is available (the message differs for Breakdown vs Trends) Try selecting a different period or breakdown type Check that you have transactions in the selected date range

heading: Spending calendar (year view)
text: Spending calendar is a full-screen year heatmap of daily spending (or income) for the same entity you opened Analytics for.

heading: How to open it
text: On the Analytics screen, tap More analytics (⋮) in the app bar Choose Spending calendar (“Daily spending for the year”) The calendar opens for the year of the Analytics end date.

heading: What it shows
text: A vertical year calendar with months in a compact two-column layout Each day cell is shaded by that day’s total amount (darker = higher) Year navigation with left/right controls in the app bar (you can move back freely; forward only up to the current year) If both expenses and income exist for the entity/year, an expenses/income dropdown switches which amounts color the calendar Empty years show “No transactions for this year”

heading: Day drill-down
text: When a day has an amount greater than zero and day navigation is available, tap the day to open its transactions. A calendar opened after drilling down retains every analytics filter and opens the matching day in the analytics Transactions view.

heading: Tips for Using Analytics
text: Start with the big picture - Use "All Time" to see overall patterns, then narrow down Compare periods - Use the period picker’s compare icon for previous period or same period last year, and also try different months/years manually Use breakdown types - Try different breakdowns to find insights: Categories show what you spend on Contacts show where you spend Tags show why you spend Check vs Income on trends - Overlay income on expense bars to see if you're living within your means in the same period Use section colors on trends - Turn on the Sections toggle to see which budget sections drive each bar Tap to drill down - Each selection narrows the current data. Choose Transactions at any level, or continue until transactions appear automatically. Open the spending calendar - Use More analytics → Spending calendar to spot high-spend days across a full year Track expense types - If you categorize expenses as Needs, Wants, and Savings, the trend view helps you balance them Use entity analytics - Open analytics from specific accounts, contacts, or tags for focused insights Watch for spikes - The trend chart and spending calendar help identify unusual spending days or months Review monthly - Regular analytics review helps you stay on track with your budget goals

heading: Common Questions
text: Why don't I see certain breakdown types? A breakdown must offer at least two different nonempty groups and must not already be selected in the navigation path. Contacts is hidden if all matching purchases have the same contact; Tags is hidden if every tag covers exactly the same purchases. When no useful grouping remains, the app shows transactions. Why are the percentages different from what I expected? Check your percentage mode. "% of Expenses" uses positive net expense totals in the breakdown; "% of Income" uses the selected income denominator. Refunds and amounts allocated across multiple tags can affect the displayed shares. Can I see analytics for a specific date range? Yes. Changing the period reloads the matching data while retaining your starting entity or set and every drill-down filter. Period comparisons apply that same selection to the comparison dates. How do I compare this month to last month or last year? Tap the compare arrows on the left of the period picker, then choose Previous period or Same period last year . Disable comparison from the same sheet when you are done. Why don't I see section colors on the trend chart? Section-colored stacked bars appear only on expense trend types when section data exists, and only after you turn on the Sections toggle (pie-chart outline icon) next to vs Income . Where is the year spending calendar? On Analytics, tap More analytics (⋮) → Spending calendar . Why are some transactions missing from analytics? Analytics uses only stored (saved) transactions in the selected date range. Preview (forecasted) transactions from recurring schedules are not included. Transfers and balance adjustments are also excluded from the analytics data.

heading: Desktop Analytics (budgetum.app/analytics)
text: Desktop Analytics is a separate, browser-based reporting experience for computers. It complements the in-app Analytics screen with larger layouts and additional reports.

heading: How to open it
text: In the app, go to More → Advanced Features → Import / Export Export your transactions (optionally enable Include analytics data to get a ZIP with transactions.csv plus analytics.json ) On a computer, open budgetum.app/analytics Choose the exported .csv or .zip file You can also open About desktop analytics from Import / Export for an in-app preview of the desktop reports, privacy notes, and a copyable link.

heading: Privacy
text: Desktop Analytics is built for desktop use and is private and offline in the browser: your chosen file is read locally, and your transaction data does not leave your device.

heading: What you can explore
text: Desktop reports include: Overview - Income, expenses, remaining money, spending mix, and cash flow in one dashboard Money flow - How money moves across accounts and related activity Breakdown - Group spending or income by section, category, contact, account, tags, and more Trends - Compare monthly income and expenses with charts and detailed hover insights Spending calendar - Monthly grids, yearly strips, and weekday patterns Categories / Contacts / Tags - Entity-focused reports with trends and related activity Sets - Use Saved Sets from your export (when analytics metadata is included) as filters Recurring - Recurring income and expenses by month, plus schedule review Capital - Net worth style view across assets, liabilities, and account groups over time Transactions - Search and inspect exported transactions

heading: CSV vs ZIP
text: CSV only - Works for transaction-based reports from transactions.csv ZIP with analytics data - Adds analytics.json so Desktop Analytics can use richer metadata (icons, colors, recurring templates, saved sets, account details, and similar export extras). Entity matching is name-based because exported entity names are treated as unique for this app For export steps, columns, and import, see the Import / Export section in the Settings documentation.

The Saved Sets screen lets you save reusable groups of transaction conditions. A set can be used to quickly open a filtered transaction list, review analytics for the matching transactions, or apply bulk changes to all matching transactions in one place. In the app, this feature is labeled "Sets" .

heading: Accessing the Saved Sets Screen
text: You can access this screen by: Going to More Opening Advanced Features Tapping Sets Note: Sets is a Pro feature.

heading: What a Saved Set Does
text: A saved set stores: An optional date range Include conditions that define which transactions should match Exclude conditions that remove unwanted transactions from the result Once saved, the set becomes a reusable filter. Instead of rebuilding the same search again and again, you can open the set and immediately work with the matching transactions. Common uses include: Reviewing all grocery spending from selected accounts Finding transactions for specific contacts or tags Building a temporary work set for cleanup or re-categorization Applying bulk changes to many matching transactions at once

heading: Screen Layout
text: The main screen shows all of your saved sets as a vertical list of cards.

heading: Help Card
text: A dismissible help card can appear at the top (and as the empty-state content when you have no sets yet). It explains building include/exclude conditions, opening matching transactions or analytics, and using mass update, with short example set ideas. Dismiss with Got it! After dismiss, an empty list shows the normal empty-state message instead Dismissal is remembered; More → Tips & Assistance → Reset Tutorial restores it

heading: Top Bar
text: The top bar contains: Sort icon - Opens the set ordering screen so you can rearrange saved sets Add icon - Creates a new saved set

heading: Saved Set Card
text: Each set card may show: Set name - The name you gave the set Link icon - A small link beside the name when the set is included on Budget Amount summary - A net total, or separate positive/negative badges when both income and expense are present Transaction count - A small number showing how many matching transactions were found Condition icons - Small icons summarizing what the set filters by Period - The saved date range, such as Jan 1 - Now More button - Opens actions for that set

heading: Condition Icons
text: The icon row gives you a quick visual summary of the filters inside the set. Section and category filters use the related section icons and colors Account filters use the account group's icon Contact filters use the contact type icon Tag filters use a tag icon Description filters use a note icon Excluded conditions are shown with a red outline so you can tell them apart from included ones.

heading: Tap a Set
text: Tapping a saved set opens a filtered transactions screen for the set's date range and conditions. Upcoming transactions can include recurring previews that match the same include/exclude conditions and amount limits. Previews are not saved transactions and do not enter the editor's matching counters or Mass Update. The Sets list's amount summaries use saved transactions; the transaction screen's Upcoming totals also include matching previews within its selected dates. This is useful when you want to: Review the matching transactions in detail Edit individual transactions Verify that the set is catching the right data

heading: Analytics for a Set
text: Choose Analytics from the set’s menu to open its matching transactions for the set’s resolved period. Each drill-down keeps the set conditions: Vacation › Groceries › Store A shows only grocery transactions at Store A that belong to Vacation. Changing the analytics dates reloads that selection without changing the saved set itself. Use the Transactions option inside analytics to inspect the matching purchases, or return through the compact breadcrumbs below the summary. See Analytics & Reports for breakdown availability, comparisons, and transaction grouping.

heading: More Menu
text: Tap the three-dot button, or long-press the card, to open these actions: Transactions - Opens the filtered transaction list Analytics - Opens analytics for the matching transactions Mass Update - Applies bulk changes to all matching transactions Edit - Changes the set's name, period, or conditions Add to Budget - Includes the set on Budget in every period, with no plan until you add one there. Shown when the set is not already on Budget. Requires Pro; otherwise the upgrade screen opens. If you upgrade and return, the set is included Unlink from Budget - Replaces Add to Budget when the set is already on Budget. Removes it from Budget in every period without deleting the set or its saved plans. Available even without Pro Delete - Removes the saved set after confirmation Deleting a set does not delete the transactions inside it. It only removes the saved filter.

heading: When an item used by a set is deleted
text: If you delete a tag, contact, category, section, or account that a set's conditions use, the set is updated automatically, without a separate warning. The deleted item is removed from those conditions. If it was the only item in a condition, that condition is removed. If the condition was the only one in its group, the group is removed too. The set then matches using its remaining conditions, so its transaction count and totals can change. For example, a set with only Tag: Trip matches all transactions (within its period and amount range) after the Trip tag is deleted. A set with has all of Trip, Hotel becomes has all of Hotel . Removing an item from an exclude condition does not change which transactions the set shows. Merging keeps sets pointing at the merged item instead.

heading: Creating or Editing a Set
text: When you create or edit a set, the screen has Include and Exclude tabs in the top bar. The rest of the screen scrolls together: name, optional period, optional amount range, then the conditions for the selected tab. The save button is the checkmark in the top bar. The ⋮ menu beside it opens Transactions , Analytics , and Mass Update for the name, period, amount, and conditions currently on the screen, including changes that are not saved. An empty name uses the create or edit title on those screens. If the end date is before the start date, the period error appears and the screen does not open. Leaving the editor without the checkmark still discards the set. Mass Update still changes the matching saved transactions. Recurring previews on Transactions → Upcoming still follow the last saved set; a set that has never been saved shows no previews.

heading: Name
text: Every set needs a name. This is the title shown in the list.

heading: Period
text: Period is optional. If no dates are set, the editor shows a compact Period chip under the name, on the same row as Amount when that filter is also unused. Tap Period to add: Start date End date Each date field has an × . If you clear a date and the other date is empty, the date fields hide and the Period chip returns. If you leave the end date empty, the set continues up to Now . If both dates are empty, the set can match transactions across all available time.

heading: Amount range
text: Amount is also optional and applies to the whole set, not to a single group. If no amount range is set, the editor shows a compact Amount chip next to Period . Tap it to add Minimum amount and Maximum amount . The collapsed amount line shows both limits with AND between them, such as >= 5 AND <= 6 . Use × to remove the amount filter even if you have not entered values yet. The Amount chip then returns.

heading: Include Tab
text: The Include tab defines what should match. Conditions are grouped: Conditions in the same group all have to match ( AND ) Separate groups are alternatives ( OR ) A new set starts with one group. Use Add condition inside a group to add another rule to that group. Use Add group to start an alternative combination. A grey OR divider appears between groups. Each group has an × on the Add condition row so you can remove it, including when there is only one group. Removing the last group leaves no include conditions, so the set can match any transaction in the period and amount range that is not excluded. Dates and the amount range stay shared constraints above the groups. They apply to the whole set, not to a single group. They are not listed in Add condition . Existing sets that used Any (OR) keep the same results: each of those conditions becomes its own group. The Include tab also shows a running count of the final matching result : transactions that satisfy any include group, the shared dates and amount range, and are not removed by Exclude. Each condition tile shows its own count instead, so you can tell a single rule apart from that combined result. The Add condition row also shows how many transactions match that group alone.

heading: Exclude Tab
text: The Exclude tab removes transactions from the result. A transaction is removed if it matches any exclusion. Use this when you want a broad include rule but need to subtract certain categories, contacts, tags, accounts, or other values. The Exclude tab count shows how many transactions match at least one exclusion in the chosen dates. Those transactions are the ones subtracted from the Include result.

heading: Available Conditions
text: You can add conditions for: Categories Sections Contacts Tags Accounts Descriptions Category types Contact types The amount range is added with the Amount chip, not from Add condition . Already used fields stay available in Add condition . Each time you add the same field, it becomes a separate condition. For example, in the same group, one Tags condition can require any of #gift or #birthday , and another Tags condition can require a name that starts with alcohol/ . Both must match. Put those conditions in different groups if either combination should be enough. Each condition tile keeps the compact outlined field, floating label, icon, count, and × button. The floating label includes a short matching summary, such as Tags · All or Descriptions · Starts with . Long summaries are shortened so they still fit small screens. Matching options are chosen inside the selector for that condition. Tap the condition tile to open it, then tap an outlined dropdown at the top to choose a matching option. Each dropdown shows only the current choice until opened. Tag dropdowns sit side by side when the translated labels and text size fit; they stack on narrower screens or with larger text. Other fields have one matching dropdown. The dropdowns, selected values, and text input share a compact form card with aligned edges. That card stays at the top of the screen, so the selected chips stay visible. Available values appear in a separate list below that scrolls on its own. The form stays put when the keyboard is open. Changes apply to the condition as you select options or values. Use Back to return to the Set editor, then use its top-right checkmark to save the Set.

heading: Tags
text: Tag conditions have two matching choices: Combine values: Any , All , or None Match names: Exactly , Starts with , Ends with , or Contains Exactly uses the existing tag checklist. For a name pattern, choose Starts with , Ends with , or Contains , type in Tag name pattern , then tap the + button beside the input or submit from the keyboard to add it. Selected patterns appear above the input. Patterns also apply to tags you create later. The list below the form previews current tag names. With an empty input it shows all names, regardless of selected patterns. As you type, it filters names using the chosen Starts with , Ends with , or Contains option, ignoring letter case. Changing that option updates the preview for the text still in the input. Tap a row to add its full tag name as a pattern using the current matching option. This clears the input and restores the full list. Tapping a name already selected does not add a duplicate or remove it; use its selected chip above to remove it. A checkmark and teal highlighting identify names already selected or covered by any selected pattern. For example, selecting Starts with and adding alcohol/ checks both alcohol/beer and alcohol/wine . Checks use saved patterns, not text you have only typed into the input. They indicate coverage by a selected pattern, regardless of Any , All , or None ; they do not indicate whether a transaction passes the complete Set. Tapping a covered row still adds its full name as a separate selected pattern. Remove patterns using the chips above. Tap + or submit from the keyboard to add the typed text as a selected pattern. This clears the input and restores the full list. Selected patterns stay above the input and do not filter this preview. Clearing the input with its × button also restores the full list without changing your selections. A no-results message appears when no names match; you can still add the typed pattern. Switching a tag-name pattern to Exactly selects the current tag names that match the previous Starts with , Ends with , or Contains option. The pattern becomes a fixed selection of those names, so newly created matching tags are no longer added automatically. Any + Exactly is the default, so existing sets keep matching the same transactions. You can also choose Is empty or Is not empty to find untagged transactions, or transactions that have at least one tag. These options hide the Combine values dropdown and value selection, since no selected tag or pattern is needed. The explanation distinguishes transactions with no tags from transactions with at least one tag.

heading: Descriptions
text: Description conditions can use existing transaction descriptions or custom text values. Matching ignores letter case and spaces at the beginning or end of descriptions and selected text. A description containing only whitespace counts as empty. The original note text is preserved. Matching options are: Contains (default, case-insensitive, same as before) Does not contain Starts with Ends with Equals Does not equal Is empty Is not empty The list below the input is a preview, showing up to 50 recent descriptions when the input is empty. Typing filters descriptions using the selected matching option, ignoring letter case; changing the option updates the preview. Tap a row to add its full description using the current matching option; this clears the input and restores recent descriptions. Tapping an already selected description keeps it selected without adding a duplicate. Tap + or submit from the keyboard to add your typed text to the selected values above. The input then clears and recent descriptions return. Selected values do not filter the preview. Clearing the input also restores recent descriptions without changing your selections. Description rows also show a checkmark and teal highlighting when their full text is selected, or when a selected Contains , Starts with , or Ends with pattern covers them. Matching ignores letter case. For Equals , Does not equal , and Does not contain , checks identify explicitly selected text only. The checkmark shows selection coverage, not the final transaction results. This is useful for catching merchants, notes, or keywords that are not covered by categories alone.

heading: Other Fields
text: Categories, sections, accounts, category types, and contact types use: Is any of (default) Is none of Contacts also include Is empty and Is not empty , so you can find transactions with no contact, or only transactions that have one.

heading: Amount Range
text: The amount range filter lets you define: Minimum amount Maximum amount Add it with the Amount chip. It applies to the whole set on both tabs. The preview uses AND between the minimum and maximum, and × removes the filter.

heading: Live Counts
text: Each active condition shows a small counter for that condition alone , using the set’s dates. The Add condition row shows that group’s count. The Include tab count is the final matching result after all include groups, exclusions, dates, and the amount range. Transaction lists, analytics, and mass update use that same final matching result, including when you open them from the editor before saving.

heading: Mass Update
text: Mass Update lets you change all transactions in a saved set together. Before applying changes, the screen shows how many transactions will be affected and warns that creating a backup is recommended. Available bulk operations include: Replacing the category Replacing or clearing the contact Adding, removing, replacing, or clearing all tags Appending to, replacing, or clearing the description Deleting all matching transactions This is especially helpful for cleanup after imports, fixing repeated mistakes, or re-labeling a large group of transactions. Note: Category replacement may be unavailable when the set contains a mix of income and expense transactions.

heading: Reordering Sets
text: Tap the Sort button in the top bar to open the Set Order screen. There you can: Drag and drop sets into your preferred order Control how sets appear on the main Saved Sets screen and the Budget Sets block When opened through Budget’s Sets block, unwatched sets appear dimmed but can still be reordered; this does not add them to Budget

heading: Empty State
text: If you have not created any sets yet, the screen shows a simple message indicating that no saved sets exist yet.

heading: Watching sets on Budget
text: Pro users can enable Budget → Display Settings → Sets → Show Sets , then use Add Set in the block. On this screen, a link icon beside the name marks a set already included on Budget. Add to Budget or Unlink from Budget in the set menu changes that without opening the plan form. The watched list is global, follows this screen's set order, and uses the selected Budget dates instead of the saved set dates. Plan amounts are entered separately for each budget period, initially empty (no plan); entering 0 saves a real zero plan. The Expense/Income plan type is shared across periods for that set. Saved planned amounts, including 0, can be copied with Copy Plan into periods with no plan. The set-item display switches are independent of category settings; only actual amounts are shown by default. Plan type selection is always available, including for sets based on tags; new sets default to Expense. Use Unlink from Budget to stop watching a set without deleting it or its plans. See Sets on Budget for adding, removing, plan comparisons, display settings, and matching transactions.

heading: Tips for Using Saved Sets
text: Start broad, then exclude - It is often easier to include a large group first and then remove edge cases with the Exclude tab. Use clear names - Good names like "Groceries - Family - This Year" make sets easy to recognize later. Check transaction counts while building - The live counts help confirm that your conditions are matching what you expect. Use sets before mass edits - Open the transaction list first to verify the results before applying bulk updates. Use amount ranges for cleanup - Amount filters are helpful when you need to find repeated charges, salary payments, or suspicious duplicates.

The Categories Screen is where you manage all your budget categories and sections. This is your master list of spending and income categories that you can use across all budgets. Categories are organized into sections (groups), making it easy to find and manage related categories together.

heading: Accessing the Categories Screen
text: You can access the Categories Screen by: Tapping More in the bottom navigation bar, then tapping Categories under Advanced Features You can also create categories directly from the Budget (main) screen without opening the Categories screen: From the Budget top-right menu (☰) -> Add Category From an expanded section -> New Income Source / New Expense Category Visual circles mode is for quick transaction entry (section circle → category bottom sheet → Add Transaction). It does not include an Add Category circle.

heading: What Are Sections?
text: Sections are groups that organize your categories. Think of them as folders or containers. For example: Housing section might contain: Rent, Utilities, Home Insurance, Repairs Transportation section might contain: Gas, Car Payment, Public Transit, Parking Food section might contain: Groceries, Restaurants, Coffee, Takeout Each section has: A custom icon A custom color One or more categories inside it

heading: What Are Categories?
text: Categories are the specific types of expenses or income you want to track. Every transaction you record is assigned to a category. Categories always belong to a section. Example categories: Groceries (in Food section) Electric Bill (in Housing section) Salary (in Income section) Netflix (in Entertainment section)

heading: Income Section
text: There is a special built-in Income section that cannot be deleted. This section contains your income categories (like Salary, Freelance, Investments). Income categories work differently from expense categories - transactions in these categories add to your balance rather than subtract from it.

heading: Section Cards
text: The main area displays your sections as expandable cards. Each section card shows: Icon - The section's custom icon (displayed in the section's color) Section name - The name of the section (e.g., "Food", "Transportation") Expand arrow - Indicates the section can be expanded to show categories Total amount - The sum of all category totals within this section (or a loading spinner while totals are calculated) Positive amounts (more income than expenses) show with a plus sign Negative amounts (more expenses than income) show as the amount spent Menu button (three dots) - Opens section actions

heading: Categories Within Sections
text: Tap or expand a section to see its categories. Each category shows: Category name - The name of the category Total amount - The transaction total for this category, or a loading spinner while it is calculated (colored to match the section) Menu button (three dots) - Opens category actions

heading: Section Colors
text: Each section has its own color. The section's border, icon, and category totals all use this color, making it easy to visually distinguish between different spending areas.

heading: Top Bar Actions

When searching: If your search matches a section name, all categories in that section are shown If your search matches a category name, only matching categories are shown (within their sections) Tap the search icon again to close the search bar and clear the search.

The Income section cannot be deleted.

To remove such a category, you would first need to reassign or remove those, or use the Merge feature to combine it with another category.

heading: Adding a New Section
text: When adding a new section, you'll set:

heading: Required Fields

heading: Optional Fields
text: Icon - Choose from a variety of icons to represent this section Color - Pick a color to identify this section visually

heading: Adding a New Category
text: When adding a new category, you'll set:

heading: Required Fields

heading: Editing a Section
text: When editing a section, you can change: Name - Update the section's display name Icon - Choose a different icon Color - Pick a new color All changes apply immediately to the section and its visual appearance throughout the app.

heading: Editing a Category
text: When editing a category, you can change: Name - Update the category's display name Section - Move the category to a different section Moving a category to another section does not affect any transactions already assigned to that category.

heading: Merging Categories
text: The Merge Categories feature lets you combine two or more categories into one. This is useful when: You've created duplicate categories by mistake You want to simplify your budget structure You want to consolidate similar categories Open Categories → More Options (three dots) → Merge Categories . Create Backup Now opens the backup screen; returning preserves the form. Opening backup hides the reminder for this visit, whether or not a backup was created. Select Categories to Merge . Choose the Target Category to keep. Choose at least one other source category; choosing only the target as a source shows a validation message. Income and expense categories cannot be merged together. The target must still exist and be active. Optionally enter Extra Description to append text to descriptions of moved transactions, select Use category name as description to fill empty descriptions with the original category name, or choose Extra Tags . Existing tags stay attached and repeated tags are not added again. These optional changes apply to moved transactions, not to favourites or recurring templates, nor to transactions already in the target category. Turning on the category-name option clears and disables Extra Description. Tap the checkmark at the top right to validate your selections and open Merge Confirmation . Cancel keeps the form open with selections and optional fields preserved. Merge Categories confirms the merge. A progress indicator replaces the form and Back is disabled until it finishes. Success returns to Categories. On failure, an error message appears and the form remains available for another attempt; no partial merge is saved. If a selection was deleted or the target archived, leave and reopen the form to select available categories. The merge moves all historical and planned transactions, favourites, and recurring templates, including inactive schedules, to the target. Transaction amounts, accounts, dates, and recurring schedules remain unchanged. The target keeps its name, section, and category type; source categories are deleted.

heading: Budget Plans
text: Source and target planned amounts are added together within each calendar month or each individual custom budget period . For example, a source plan of 20, another source plan of 30, and an existing target plan of 100 in January become one target plan of 150 for January. February remains separate. Custom periods remain separate even if their date ranges overlap or are identical, and are never combined with calendar-month plans. If the target has no plan for a source's month or period, that source plan moves to the target. Zero amounts are preserved as plans, not removed. The target section is included in each affected month or custom period where needed so the moved plan can be shown. Existing section plans and the custom period's overall budget settings remain unchanged. Source plan amounts are no longer discarded.

heading: Saved Sets, Import Rules, and Hidden Notes
text: Saved Sets: source category selections change to the target in both included and excluded category filters, with duplicates removed within each list. Section and category-type filters remain unchanged. Results may therefore change, especially when the target belongs to another section or category type. If the target ends up both included and excluded, exclusion still applies; review the set's filters afterward. Statement imports: remembered category choices change to the target, so future matching imports can use it. Hidden note suggestions: hidden descriptions from the sources remain hidden under the target, with identical entries combined. Existing target preferences remain. Hiding applies to the exact saved text; using Extra Description changes transaction text and does not create a hidden preference for the new wording. This action cannot be undone from the merge screen. Create a backup before merging if you may need the original categories and plans. Back before confirmation leaves the categories unchanged; reopening starts a new form.

heading: Changing Order
text: From the Order screen, you can customize how sections and categories are displayed:

heading: Reordering Sections
text: Drag sections up or down to change their display order The order you set here is used throughout the app

heading: Reordering Categories
text: Within each section, drag categories to change their order This affects how categories appear in dropdown menus and lists

heading: No Categories Yet
text: If you haven't created any sections or categories, you'll see a helpful message with an "Add Section" button to get started. This typically only happens when you first install the app before setting up your budget.

heading: No Search Results
text: If your search doesn't match any sections or categories, you'll see a message indicating no categories were found.

heading: Empty Section
text: If a section has no categories, you'll see an "Add Category" button inside the expanded section to help you get started.

heading: Tips for Organizing Categories
text: When picking a category elsewhere (for example Add Transaction), sections or categories that are hidden for the current budget period can be revealed with Show more (+N) in the category picker. On the Budget screen’s visual circles section sheet, the same control can reveal hidden category circles. Use meaningful section groups - Group categories that make sense together. This makes it easier to analyze spending by area (e.g., all food-related expenses in one section). Don't over-categorize - Having too many categories can make tracking transactions tedious. Find a balance that gives you useful insights without being overwhelming. Use specific names - Category names like "Electric" and "Gas" are more useful than just "Bills" when reviewing your spending. Review periodically - As your spending habits change, you may want to add new categories, merge unused ones, or reorganize sections. Use the Analytics feature - After you've been tracking for a while, use the Analytics option on sections and categories to gain insights into your spending patterns. Consider the transaction flow - When creating new transactions, you'll choose from these categories. Organize them in an order that makes quick selection easy. Use merge for cleanup - If you find you've been using two categories for the same type of expense, use Merge to combine them and consolidate your history.

heading: Categories vs. Tags
text: Categories and tags both help organize transactions, but they work differently. Categories answer “What type of spending or income is this?” They are required: every transaction has exactly one category. Categories live in sections, shape your budget, and are used for planning and reports. Use them for the main classification (e.g. Groceries, Rent, Salary). Tags answer “How do I want to slice or group this later?” They are optional: you can add none, one, or many tags to a transaction. Tags are a flat list and can be used for anything—projects, events, people, or custom groupings. Use them for cross-category tracking (e.g. all spending tagged “Vacation” or “Home office”). Example: A dinner at a restaurant while on vacation: Category: "Restaurants" (in Food section) — so it appears in your Food budget. Tags: "Vacation 2024", "Italy Trip" — so you can see total vacation or trip spending across all categories. Together, categories keep your budget structured; tags let you ask flexible questions across that structure.

The Contacts Screen is where you manage all the people and businesses you transact with. Contacts help you track who you're paying money to or receiving money from, making it easy to see your spending patterns with specific stores, companies, or individuals over time.

heading: Accessing the Contacts Screen

heading: Understanding Contact Categories
text: Contacts are organized into categories to help you find and group them logically. The available categories are: Stores - Physical retail locations where you shop Online Stores - E-commerce websites and online retailers Cafes & Restaurants - Places where you eat and drink Individuals - People you transact with (friends, family, freelancers) Companies & Organizations - Businesses and organizations Healthcare - Doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, and health services Investments - Brokerages, investment platforms, and financial institutions Charity - Non-profits and charitable organizations Other - Anything that doesn't fit the categories above Each category displays its own icon and groups all related contacts together.

heading: Contact Category Cards
text: The main area displays your contacts organized into category cards. Each card shows: Category icon (on the left) - A visual identifier for the category type Category name - The name of the category (e.g., "Stores", "Individuals") Contacts within - All contacts belonging to that category, listed alphabetically

heading: Individual Contacts

heading: Adding a New Contact

heading: Required Fields

heading: Optional Fields

heading: Editing a Contact

heading: Merging Contacts
text: Open More → Contacts , tap the three dots in the top bar , then Merge Contacts . This action is available without Pro, including when the list is empty or only one contact exists; completing a merge requires at least two distinct existing contacts and an active target. Read the backup reminder. Create Backup Now opens the backup screen. Return with Back to continue with your selections preserved. Opening backup hides the reminder for this visit; it does not confirm that a backup was created. Tap Contacts to Merge . This opens the usual Contacts selection page. Both the source and target pickers use this title. Contacts are grouped by contact category and sorted alphabetically within each group. Active and archived entries appear, with an archive icon beside archived entries. Tap a row to select or deselect it; selected rows are highlighted and show a checkmark. Tap the search icon in the top bar to search names or descriptions. The selected-item strip stays visible while filtering: tap an item in the strip to remove it, or the × at the right to clear the selection. Closing search clears the search text but preserves selections. Selection changes apply to the merge form immediately, including removing or clearing selections. Use Back to return with your current selection preserved; there is no approval checkmark in the picker. Selecting items alone does not perform a merge. Tap Target Contact and then tap the existing contact you want to keep. This field is disabled until a source is selected. Only active contacts appear as targets. The target may also be in the source selection, but at least one other source is required. Clearing all sources also clears the target. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the merge form. Missing sources or a missing target show a validation message; selecting only the target as a source is also rejected. Review the confirmation, which shows the number of sources that will be deleted (excluding the target) and the target's name. Cancel returns to the form with selections preserved. Merge Contacts confirms the permanent merge. While it runs, the form shows a progress indicator and Back is disabled. Success returns to the Contacts list with a success message and refreshed totals. The merge affects all dates , including historical and planned transactions, favourites, and recurring transactions, even inactive schedules. Source contacts are deleted. The target keeps its name, description, and contact category. Transaction amounts, dates, descriptions, accounts, and recurring schedules stay the same. There are no extra-description or extra-tag options on this form. All transactions using a source contact now use the target contact. Remembered contact choices for statement imports also change to the target, so future matching imports can use it. Saved Sets replace source contact selections with the target in both included and excluded filters, removing repeated selections within each list. This can change results: a filter now covers the combined contact's transactions. If the merge leaves the target both included and excluded, exclusion still applies; review the Saved Set filters afterward. If a picker has no matching entries, it shows the usual contact search empty state. Clear or close search, or return with Back. Use + in either picker to create a contact with the usual Add form. Saving from the source picker selects the new contact immediately and keeps the picker open; use Back to return to the merge form. Saving from the target picker selects the new target and returns to the merge form. Back from Add without saving preserves the existing selection. Newly created contacts remain available even if you later cancel the merge. Pickers load the current list when opened. If loading fails, return and reopen the picker. If a merge fails, an error message appears and selections remain. Correct unavailable sources or targets by reopening the relevant picker; a target must be active. This action cannot be undone from the merge screen. Back before confirmation does not merge or delete anything; newly created entries remain; returning later starts with empty selections. A backup made before merging is the recovery option if you need the original records.

heading: Tips for Using Contacts
text: Be consistent with naming - Use the same spelling for the same business or person to keep your data clean Choose the right category - Proper categorization makes it easier to find contacts and understand your spending patterns Use descriptions wisely - Add helpful notes like location, account numbers, or what you typically buy there Check the Contact Summary Period - Make sure you understand which time period the displayed totals represent (Settings → Contact Summary Period) Archive instead of delete - If you stop transacting with a contact, archive it to keep your history intact Review analytics - Use the Analytics option (when the contact has transactions) to see detailed charts and breakdowns of your spending with specific contacts Use search for quick access - When you have many contacts, the search feature helps you find what you need quickly Link contacts to transactions - When adding transactions, assign them to contacts to build useful spending insights over time Regular cleanup - Periodically review your contacts and archive any you no longer use to keep your list manageable

The Tags Screen is where you manage all your tags for organizing and labeling transactions. Tags provide a flexible way to categorize your spending and income beyond the standard budget categories. For example, you might use tags like "Vacation", "Business Trip", "Gift", or "Reimbursable" to track spending across different contexts.

Example uses for tags: Track all expenses for a specific vacation or trip Mark transactions as business-related for expense reports Label gift purchases during holidays Identify reimbursable expenses Group transactions for a specific project or event You can add multiple tags to a single transaction, giving you powerful flexibility in organizing your financial data.
