text: For archived tags, you can: View Transactions - See the tag's transaction history View Trends - See year-by-year totals for this tag Restore - Bring the tag back to your main list (only available if the tag has transactions) Delete - Permanently remove the tag (only available if the tag has no transactions)

heading: No Tags Yet
text: If you haven't created any tags, you'll see a helpful message with an "Add Tag" button to get started.

heading: No Search Results
text: If your search doesn't match any tags, you'll see a message indicating no tags were found, along with an option to add a new tag.

heading: Pro Version Benefits
text: The free version of Budgetum limits you to 5 tags. With Budgetum Pro, you get: Unlimited tags - Create as many tags as you need A banner on the Tags Screen shows your current limit status in the free version

heading: Tips for Using Tags
text: Use tags for cross-category tracking - Tags work best when they span multiple budget categories (e.g., a "Vacation" tag might include flights, hotels, food, and entertainment) Be specific with names - Include dates or details in tag names like "Italy Trip 2024" instead of just "Vacation" Add helpful descriptions - Use the description field to add context you might forget later Review analytics - Use the Analytics option to see detailed charts and breakdowns of your spending patterns for specific tags Check the totals period - Make sure you understand which time period the displayed totals represent Archive completed projects - When a trip ends or a project finishes, archive the tag to keep your active list clean while preserving history Use multiple tags - You can add several tags to a single transaction for maximum flexibility (e.g., a business dinner could have both "Client Meeting" and "Business Trip" tags) Combine with contacts - Use tags alongside contacts for powerful tracking (e.g., see all "Reimbursable" expenses at a specific store)

The Settings screen is your central hub for customizing Budgetum to work the way you want. Here you can personalize the app's appearance, manage your data, access advanced features, and find help resources. In the app, this screen is labeled "More" in the bottom navigation and in the screen header (the tab and title both say "More").

heading: Accessing the Settings Screen
text: You can access this screen by: Tapping the "More" tab in the bottom navigation If you have upgraded to Budgetum Pro, a gold "Pro" badge will appear next to "More" in the header. A small dot can appear on the More tab when a rating or feedback invitation is ready. Closing the rating card on Budget clears the rating-related dot but leaves the rating card available in More. A separate eligible feedback invitation can still show the dot.

heading: Screen Layout
text: The Settings screen is organized into sections, each presented as a card with related options: Upgrade to Pro (only shown if you haven't upgraded yet) Advanced Features - Access to powerful tools for organizing your finances Appearance - Customize how the app looks Localization - Language, currency, and number formatting preferences Tips & Assistance - Tutorial, assistant, and quick video tips About - App information, feedback, and legal links Official Links - Budgetum website and community/support links Other - Extra features and fun tools

heading: Upgrade to Pro
text: If you're using the free version, the first card invites you to upgrade to Budgetum Pro.

heading: What You Get with Pro
text: Tapping this option opens the Pro upgrade page, which explains the benefits: Support Development - Your purchase helps fund continued app development and new features More Features - Pro users get access to optional and additional features; tap List to see examples such as more than 5 recurring transactions, more than 5 tags, bank statement matching, and Saved Sets Limited Time Pricing - Early supporters get the best price

heading: Making the Purchase
text: The upgrade is a one-time payment (not a subscription) Tap the upgrade button to purchase through the App Store After purchase, the "Pro" badge appears throughout the app The upgrade card disappears from Settings once you're a Pro user

heading: Restore Purchases
text: If you've already purchased Pro (perhaps on another device), tap Restore Purchases on the Budgetum Pro card to restore your Pro status without paying again.

heading: Advanced Features
text: This section provides quick access to powerful organizational tools.

heading: Backup
text: Protect your financial data by creating backups. Tapping this option opens the Backup page with two main functions: Export Backup Tap Export Data to create a backup file of all your data Opens a share sheet so you can save the file to cloud storage (iCloud, Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.), email it to yourself, or save it anywhere you prefer The backup file is named with the date (e.g., BUDGETUM_2024-01-15.backup ) Records when you last created a backup Restore from Backup Tap Restore Data to restore data from a previously created backup file Select a .backup file from your device or cloud storage Important: Importing a backup replaces ALL your current data - you'll be asked to confirm before proceeding Use this to restore data or transfer your information to a new device Backup Reminders The Settings screen shows your last backup date If it's been more than 60 days since your last backup (and you've been using the app for at least 32 days), the backup option will appear highlighted to remind you to back up your data

heading: Import / Export
text: Open Import / Export to export transactions as CSV (or a desktop-analytics ZIP), or to import transactions from a Budgetum CSV or another app's CSV. The screen title is Import / Export . At the top of the page, a Columns Explanation section documents every export column and transaction type. Use it as the reference when editing a CSV before import. Export Export your transaction history for spreadsheets or for Budgetum Desktop Analytics. Period options: All time - Every transaction ever recorded Month - A specific month (pick the month after choosing this option) Year - A specific year (pick the year after choosing this option) Custom period - Transactions between a start date and an end date you choose Include analytics data: When this checkbox is off, Export CSV shares a single .csv file When it is on, Export CSV shares a .zip named like a Budgetum analytics package. The ZIP contains: transactions.csv - the same transaction export analytics.json - extra metadata for Desktop Analytics (categories, contacts, tags, accounts, recurring templates, saved sets, and related display data) Desktop analytics: After export, use the file at budgetum.app/analytics on a computer The site reads the file locally in your browser; transaction data does not leave your device Tap About desktop analytics on this screen for a short in-app preview of the desktop reports, privacy notes, and a copyable link to https://budgetum.app/analytics Export columns (CSV): id - Portable transaction ID. Keep this column to avoid duplicate transactions during import date - Date in YYYY-MM-DD format amount - Budget amount: income positive, expense negative; 0 for transfers and balance rows from_amount / to_amount - Amounts debited from / credited to the related accounts type - expense , income , offset_income , transfer , balance , or initial_balance description - Short note section / category - Section and category names contact - Contact name (payee/payer) from_account_group / from_account / to_account_group / to_account - Account group and account names tags - Semicolon-separated tags (for example Food;Delivery ) receipt_id - Receipt identifier used to group receipt lines category_type - Expense category type: needs , wants , or savings (empty for income and other types) section_icon / section_color - Material icon name and hex color for the section contact_type - Contact type key (for example stores , companies , individuals ) from_account_group_icon / to_account_group_icon - Material icon names for account groups from_account_currency / to_account_currency - Currency codes of the related accounts currency - Currency of the budget amount (from-account for expenses, to-account for income, main currency as fallback) is_recurring - true if created from a recurring template; empty otherwise count - How many units a receipt line represents. On import, this is used only when the row has a receipt id. Other rows are stored with count 1, and the amount is not multiplied by count Import You can import a Budgetum CSV export, or a CSV from another app after matching columns. Budgetum transaction IDs skip rows that already exist; other CSV files are imported as new transactions after preview. Before you import: Create a backup first. Import creates transactions and new entities in bulk, and imported transactions cannot be undone automatically The import screen offers Create backup and explains that a backup is recommended Choosing a file: Tap Choose CSV file Budgetum analyzes the file Follow the path that matches the file type Budgetum CSV export: Recognized by Budgetum export headers Rows whose id already exists are skipped New rows can create missing sections, categories, contacts, tags, account groups, and accounts by name You get a preview (counts to create/skip, invalid rows, new entities), can open a transactions preview, then confirm Import transactions YNAB Register.csv: If Budgetum detects a YNAB register export, you can choose: Use YNAB import mode - Imports the register directly and pairs rows such as Transfer : Savings into one transfer Inflows categorized as Inflow: Ready to Assign (older exports: To be Budgeted ) become income in an Income category in your income section (the category and section are created if missing), with the payee as the contact Inflows in YNAB's Income category group become income in the same category name (for example Income: Salary → Salary ) Any other inflow (money returned to an expense category, such as a store refund) becomes a refund in that category, so it reduces that category's spending instead of counting as income Starting Balance rows become the account's opening balance, not income; starting balances of 0 are skipped Use generic mapping - Treats the file like any other external CSV and lets you match columns yourself Other CSV files (generic mapping): Match columns - Map your file's columns to Budgetum fields Preview - Review what will be created, skipped, or flagged Result - See created / skipped / invalid counts after import Required mapping fields: Date column - Transaction date (common date formats are accepted) Amount type - How amounts are signed in your file: Signed amount (+/-) - Positive = income, negative = expense Not signed (expense by default) - Positive amounts treated as expenses Not signed (income by default) - Positive amounts treated as income Credit and debit columns - Separate money-in and money-out columns Amount column (or credit/debit columns, depending on amount type) Category column - Required for budget rows. Empty category rows become transfers when both transfer accounts are present, or balance adjustments when a single account is present Optional mapping fields: Description, section, contact, tags, and a single account column File contains transfers - When enabled, also map source and destination account columns. Rows with both transfer accounts and no category become plain transfers; rows with a category stay budget transactions How Budgetum interprets mapped rows: Expenses and income are detected from amount direction (and your amount-type choice) Missing expense sections can fall back to an Imported section New accounts can be placed under an Imported account group when group data is missing Invalid rows must be fixed (or remapped) before import; you can open an issues review that shows mapped Budgetum values per problem row After import: Summary shows created, skipped (existing ID), and invalid counts Warnings may appear (for example an unrecognized contact type falling back to Stores) You can pick another file and run again

heading: Recurring Transactions
text: Manage your recurring transactions - repeating income and expenses that happen on a regular schedule. View all your recurring transaction templates Create new recurring transactions Edit or delete existing ones See when each recurring transaction is scheduled next For more details, see the Recurring Transactions documentation.

heading: Contacts

heading: Global Categories

View all global categories organized by sections Add new categories Edit category names and icons Delete unused categories Global categories appear in every budget, making it easy to maintain consistent tracking.

heading: Tags
text: Manage tags for organizing and filtering your transactions. View all your tags Create new tags Edit or delete existing tags Tags let you add flexible labels to transactions beyond categories, like "vacation", "business", or "gift".

heading: Sets
text: Saved Sets lets you store reusable transaction conditions so you can quickly reopen the same filtered group of transactions later. This option is available in Budgetum Pro. Create named sets of include and exclude conditions Limit sets to a custom date range or leave them open-ended Open transactions or analytics for the matching results Apply bulk updates to all matching transactions This is especially useful for repeated analysis, cleanup after imports, and large-scale transaction edits.

heading: Appearance
text: Customize how Budgetum looks to match your preferences.

heading: Theme Mode
text: Choose how the app appears: Light - Bright background with dark text Dark - Dark background with light text (easier on the eyes in low light) System - Automatically matches your device's appearance setting Your current selection is shown next to the option.

heading: Primary Color
text: Choose the accent color used throughout the app for buttons, highlights, and important elements. Tap to open a grid of color options Select any color from the palette The color is applied immediately throughout the app A checkmark indicates your current selection

heading: Localization
text: Configure language, currency, and number formatting to match your region and preferences.

heading: Language
text: Set the language used throughout the app. Available Languages: English Українська (Ukrainian) Русский (Russian) Deutsch (German) Português (Portuguese) Français (French) Español (Spanish) Your current language is shown next to the option.

heading: Currency
text: Set your primary (main) currency. This is the default currency used for new accounts and transactions. Search for any currency by name or code Popular currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, UAH, PLN) appear at the top Each currency shows its symbol and international code Your current selection is marked with a checkmark Note: This sets your default currency. Individual accounts can still use different currencies for tracking foreign accounts. Changing the main currency: Budgetum asks for confirmation ( Change Main Currency? ). Existing budget amounts keep their numbers and are only shown in the new currency—they are not converted . Account balances stay in each account’s own currency.

heading: Number Format
text: Choose how numbers are displayed throughout the app. Available Formats: System - Uses your device's regional settings 1,234.56 - Comma for thousands, dot for decimals (US/UK style) 1.234,56 - Dot for thousands, comma for decimals (European style) 1 234,56 - Space for thousands, comma for decimals 1 234.56 - Space for thousands, dot for decimals 1234.56 - No thousands separator, dot for decimals 1234,56 - No thousands separator, comma for decimals Your current format is previewed next to the option.

heading: Hide Currency Symbol
text: Toggle this option to hide currency symbols throughout the app. When on , amounts display as just numbers (e.g., "1,234.56") When off , amounts include the currency symbol (e.g., "$1,234.56") This is useful if you only use one currency and find the symbols distracting.

heading: Hide Numbers
text: Toggle this option to hide all monetary amounts in the app. When on , amounts are hidden (useful for privacy when someone might see your screen) When off , amounts display normally This is a quick privacy feature - turn it on before showing your phone to someone, then turn it off when you're done.

That hint appears again when you open Recurring Transactions with a nonempty Favourites list, even if you previously dismissed it or used the long-press shortcut. heading: About

heading: Rate App
text: Opens the App Store review form on iOS or the Google Play app listing on Android. On Android, find Rate this app and select the stars. You can return to Budgetum without submitting a rating. Your feedback helps other users discover Budgetum Reviews and ratings help prioritize new features Takes just a moment to share your experience Budgetum shows an Enjoying Budgetum? card near the top of More after either at least 10 saved transactions or 7 elapsed days since the recorded first-open date. For existing installations, that date may have been initialized from the earliest saved transaction. The count is app-wide, not limited to the selected budget period. The invitation is available to both free and Pro users, unless a previous rating invitation was dismissed or its rating action was used. The same card appears on Budget below the summary (or at the top of the scrollable content if the summary is hidden). Its × / Close button permanently hides it on Budget and clears the rating-related More dot. The More card remains available and has no close button. Changing budget periods or restarting the app does not restore the Budget card. Tapping Rate App on either card opens the store as described above and hides both cards after the store link opens successfully. This does not mean a rating was submitted: returning without rating still leaves both cards hidden. If opening the store fails, an error message appears and the invitation remains available. The regular Rate App row in More remains available; using it also hides the invitation cards. After about 50 days since the recorded first-open date — and only once the More rating card is no longer eligible — More may show a You've been using Budgetum for a long time feedback card instead. It opens email with a short template via Tell me and can be dismissed with the × in the top right. Closing only the Budget rating card does not make this feedback card appear while the More rating card is still eligible. The rating and feedback cards never appear together in More.

heading: Say thanks
text: On iOS and Android, open More → About → Say thanks , directly below Rate App . The heart row is available to both free and Pro users and opens a bottom sheet for optional tips to the developer. The sheet introduces Danylo Rudenko, who has been building Budgetum on his own in Ukraine for over two years. The sheet introduces Danylo Rudenko, who has been building Budgetum on his own in Ukraine for over two years. Choose one of four tip amounts, based on USD $1, $3, $5, and $10. The buttons display the store's actual localized prices; your Budgetum currency and Hide Numbers / Hide Currency Symbol settings do not change purchase prices. No amount is preselected. Tap a price to open the App Store or Google Play purchase confirmation. Each tip is a separate, one-time payment; it does not unlock Pro or any additional features. You can tip again later. When you open the sheet, a progress indicator appears while prices load. On Android, Budgetum also checks for any unfinished tips before enabling a new purchase. Only amounts available from the store are offered. If prices or the purchase check are unavailable, Try again retries them. A previously paid tip can still finish even if its price cannot currently be loaded. While a payment is pending, the amount buttons are disabled. You can close the sheet; closing it does not cancel a payment already submitted to the store. Cancel through the store confirmation to return to the amount choices. If the store confirmation has closed but the sheet still shows a progress indicator, close and reopen Say thanks . Budgetum checks for outstanding purchases before returning to the amounts; a pending payment or a paid tip that still needs processing remains protected from another purchase. If Google Play confirms that a previously pending payment is no longer outstanding, the amounts become available again. A successful tip shows Thank you! and a personal thank-you message. Close the sheet to return to More. If the payment finishes after you close the sheet, reopening Say thanks during the same app session shows the thank-you message. If a purchase fails, an error appears and you can try again. If the store reports payment received but processing could not finish, Try again finishes that existing purchase without charging again; new tips are disabled until it finishes. Close the sheet by swiping down or by tapping outside it. Reopening after dismissing the thank-you message offers the amounts again. Tips do not create budget transactions. Completed tips are not restored as Pro purchases, and the tip sheet has no Restore Purchases button.

heading: Snake Game (BETA)

Idea: Classic Snake with a twist: the food tries to run away from you. Move the snake, chase and eat the three food types (meet the quotas at the top), avoid walls and your tail. You have 3 lives; the game gets faster as you eat. Use swipe or on-screen D-pad (switch in the ⋮ menu when paused). Just for fun.

heading: Tips for Using Settings
text: Back up regularly - Create backups at least monthly, or before making major changes. Store backups in cloud storage for safekeeping. Try different themes - Dark mode is easier on the eyes at night and can save battery on phones with OLED screens. Match your region - Set your language, currency, and number format to match your local conventions for the most natural experience. Use the privacy toggle - The "Hide Numbers" option is perfect when you're in public and don't want others to see your balances. Export for analysis - Use Import / Export to download a CSV for spreadsheets, or enable Include analytics data and open the ZIP at budgetum.app/analytics on a computer (the file is read locally in the browser). Restore purchases on new devices - If you upgrade your phone, remember to restore your Pro purchase rather than buying again. Check for updates - Look at the version number occasionally and update the app from the App Store for the latest features and fixes. Join the community - The Reddit community is a great place to learn tips from other users and suggest features.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
text: This guide explains the common interface elements that appear throughout Budgetum. Understanding these components will help you navigate the app more efficiently as they work the same way wherever you encounter them.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Date Picker
text: The Date Picker is a powerful calendar component used whenever you need to select a date in the app—whether setting a transaction date, choosing a report period, or navigating to view transactions on a specific day.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Opening the Date Picker
text: The Date Picker opens as a panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen. You'll encounter it when: Tapping a date field in transaction forms Selecting a date range for reports Navigating to a specific day in various screens

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Navigation Levels
text: The Date Picker has three viewing levels that you can navigate between: Years View: Shows a grid of 12 years at a time Each year tile displays: The year number Total income for that year (in the income color with + prefix) Total expenses for that year (in red with - prefix) Use the left and right arrows to move between 12-year groups The current year has a special highlighted border Future years appear slightly faded Tap a year to drill down to the months within that year Months View: Shows all 12 months of the selected year The header displays: Navigation arrows to move between years The year number (tap to go back to Years View) Total income and expenses for the year Each month tile displays: The month name Total income for that month (in the income color with + prefix) Total expenses for that month (in red with - prefix) The current month has a special highlighted border Future months appear slightly faded Tap a month to drill down to the days within that month A "Select Full Year" option may appear at the top to select the entire year as a date range Days View: Shows a traditional calendar grid for the selected month The header displays: Navigation arrows to move between months The month and year (tap to go back to Months View) Total income and expenses for the month Weekday headers (Mon, Tue, Wed, etc.) appear above the grid Each day tile displays: The day number Total income for that day (in the income color with + prefix, if any) Total expenses for that day (in red with - prefix, if any) Today's date has a special highlighted border The currently selected date has a colored background Future days appear slightly faded Tap any day to select it and close the picker A "Today" or "Select Full Month" button may appear at the top

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Quick Actions
text: Today Button - Quickly jump to and select today's date Select Full Month - Select the entire current month as a date range Select Full Year - Select the entire current year as a date range

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Visual Indicators
text: The Date Picker provides helpful visual feedback: Income totals show in the income color with a + prefix Expense totals show in red with a - prefix Currently selected dates have a colored background Today has a special border even when not selected Future dates appear slightly faded

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Number Picker (Calculator)
text: The Number Picker is a calculator-style keypad that appears whenever you need to enter an amount in Budgetum. It supports basic math operations, making it easy to split bills or calculate totals right where you need them.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Opening the Number Picker
text: The Number Picker slides up from the bottom when you: Tap an amount field in any transaction form Enter a budget amount Tap a category's planned amount directly on the Budget screen for a quick plan adjustment (only when Quick plan update is on in Budget Display Settings) Set a transfer amount Enter any monetary value in the app

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Display Area
text: The top section shows: Title (optional) - Context about what you're entering (e.g., "Amount") Expression history - When performing calculations, shows the full expression (e.g., "50 × 2 =") Current value - The main number display, showing your input or calculation result Tap the display to select the entire number—this makes it easy to replace the current value entirely by simply typing a new number. Some places can show an extra quick-select action above the keypad. For example, when editing a category's planned amount from the Budget screen, Budgetum can offer the category's actual spent amount as a one-tap value so you can quickly align the plan with reality.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Keypad Layout
text: The keypad is organized in rows: Top Row (Functions): C (Clear) - Clears the entire input and starts fresh % (Percent) - Calculates percentages ± (Plus/Minus) - Toggles between positive and negative values (when allowed) ÷ (Divide) - Division operation Number Rows: Standard calculator layout with 7, 8, 9 in the first row 4, 5, 6 in the second row 1, 2, 3 in the third row Operation Keys: × (Multiply) - Multiplication operation − (Subtract) - Subtraction operation + (Add) - Addition operation Bottom Row: Decimal separator (. or , depending on your regional settings) 0 - Zero digit ⌫ (Backspace) - Deletes the last digit or cancels the current operation ✓ (Confirm) - Confirms the value and closes the picker

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Performing Calculations
text: The Number Picker supports chained calculations: Enter the first number Tap an operation (+, −, ×, ÷) Enter the second number The result preview appears dimmed Tap another operation to continue calculating, or ✓ to confirm Example: Calculating a tip Enter restaurant bill: 50 Tap × (multiply) Enter 0.15 (for 15%) See the preview: 7.50 Tap ✓ to confirm Using Percentages: For addition/subtraction: 100 + 10% = 110 (adds 10% of 100) For multiplication/division: 100 × 10% = 10 (multiplies by 0.1) Without operation: 50% = 0.5 (divides by 100)

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Visual Feedback
text: Active operation - The currently active operation button (+, −, ×, ÷) is highlighted Selection highlight - When the display is tapped to select, a subtle background indicates selection mode Pending calculation - Shows the expression and a dimmed preview of the result

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Undo
text: Press backspace (⌫) to: Delete the last digit when entering a number Cancel the current operation when one is pending Clear the selection when the display is selected

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Budget Period Picker
text: The Budget Period Picker is a full-screen selector used specifically on the Budget screen. Unlike the general Period Picker, it switches the app between monthly budgeting and saved custom budget periods.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Opening the Budget Period Picker
text: Open it by tapping the current period in the Budget screen header.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Header Toggle
text: The top bar contains a two-part toggle: Month - Standard calendar-month budgeting Other Periods - Saved custom budget periods If the Other Periods tab is active, an Add button appears in the header so you can create a new custom period.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Month Tab

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Other Periods Tab

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls

When a calendar month is selected, it opens the month editor (optional Budget amount and Income section ). See Budget Screen and Custom Budget Periods .

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Period Picker

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Appearance
text: The Period Picker appears as a horizontal bar with: Left Arrow (<) - Move to the previous period Start Date Box - Tap to set the start date Dash separator - Visual separator between dates End Date Box - Tap to set the end date Right Arrow (>) - Move to the next period Dropdown Arrow - Opens quick period options

heading: Manual Date Selection

heading: Summary Card
text: The Summary Card displays financial totals at a glance. You'll find it on budget screens, transaction lists, and detail pages for accounts, categories, and contacts.

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Basic Layout
text: The Summary Card shows three columns: Income - Total money received (shown in the income color) Expenses - Total money spent (shown in blue or red depending on context) Balance - The difference (income minus expenses)

page: Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls
heading: Budget Mode
text: When viewing budget-related screens, the Summary Card shows both planned and actual amounts: For each column: Planned amount - Your budget target (shown in gray) Actual amount - What you've actually spent/received (shown in color) Difference - How much you're over or under plan Progress indicators appear as vertical bars between columns: The bar fills up as actual approaches planned At the plan, the bar is full. Above the plan, its full length represents the actual total: the planned share keeps its normal color, while the excess is red for expenses or lighter green for income. A thin divider marks the boundary, with no minimum excess size. For example, 500 planned and 1,000 actual gives two equal portions. Expense progress uses the primary color for the planned share. The Savings breakdown uses the income color and lighter green surplus, like income. In Budget and Edit Plan summaries, progress requires planned values to be enabled and a positive actual amount. A zero or missing plan does not hide progress: expenses show fully red, while income and Savings show fully in the income color, without a divider. This applies to vertical summary bars, single-line bars, and the expanded type bars. Zero or negative actual amounts have no progress fill. Actual-only summaries on Transactions, Analytics, and Account screens do not show budget progress bars. Summary indicators use the summary’s own planned totals, including the optional category-overspending adjustment in Budget screens. See Summary Card for details.

heading: Single-Line Mode
text: When only income or only expenses exist, the Summary Card switches to a compact single-line layout: Label on the left Values on the right Progress bar below (when comparing actual to planned)

heading: Bottom Sheets
text: Bottom Sheets are panels that slide up from the bottom of the screen to present options, forms, or additional information. They're used extensively throughout Budgetum for focused interactions.

heading: Common Features
text: All bottom sheets share these characteristics: Drag handle - A small bar at the top indicating you can drag to dismiss Pull down to close - Swipe down on the sheet to dismiss it Tap outside to close - Tap the dimmed area above the sheet to close it Safe area - Content stays above the home indicator on modern devices

heading: Types of Bottom Sheets
text: Options Sheets: Present a list of actions you can take, such as: Edit, duplicate, or delete a transaction Quick period selection options Account action menus Form Sheets: Contain input fields and controls for: Date selection Number entry Configuration options Confirmation Sheets: Ask you to confirm an action, particularly for: Confirming scheduled transactions Managing recurring transactions

heading: Transaction Options Sheet
text: When you long-press or tap on a transaction, an options sheet appears with: Edit - Open the transaction for editing Edit receipt - Shown when the transaction belongs to a receipt. Opens that receipt with all of its items Duplicate - Create a copy with today's date Transform to Receipt - Convert an expense into a multi-item receipt. Hidden when the transaction is already part of a receipt Delete - Remove the transaction (with confirmation) The available options may vary based on the transaction type (regular, transfer, balance adjustment).

heading: Tips for Using Shared Components
text: Learn the gestures - Bottom sheets dismiss with a swipe down; tapping outside also closes most overlays Use the calculator - Don't switch apps to calculate—use the built-in math operations in the Number Picker Check visual indicators - Colors consistently mean the same thing: income color for income, red for over-budget or negative Expand for details - Look for the small info icon on Summary Cards indicating more details are available Use quick period options - The Period Picker's preset options save time for common date ranges Navigate Date Picker levels - Tap the header in the Date Picker to navigate up a level (days → months → years) Preview before confirming - The Number Picker shows calculation results before you confirm Use quick-select values when offered - If a suggested value appears above the keypad, tap it to replace the current number immediately. Budgetum is built around one idea: understanding your money matters more than following rules. You make a plan, record what actually happens, look at the difference, and adjust. This page explains the principles behind the app and why some things work the way they do.

heading: Why Budgetum Exists
text: Many budgeting apps try to teach a "correct" way to manage money. They push rigid rules, ask for an account or a bank connection before you can start, or put core features behind a subscription. For many people, this creates stress instead of clarity. Budgetum started as a digital version of a paper budget: write down what you expect to spend next month, then mark what really happens. It is designed to adapt to how people actually live, earn, and spend, not the other way around.

heading: No Single "Right" Way to Budget
text: Budgetum does not enforce a budgeting method. You can: Use zero-based budgeting, the 50/30/20 rule, or envelope-style accounts Plan loosely without strict limits Track expenses without planning anything Focus only on the categories that matter to you Ignore accounts, tags, contacts, and receipts if you don't need them Expense types (Needs, Wants, Savings) add structure when it helps, for example when you are learning to budget, without forcing a method on anyone. All of these approaches are valid. Budgetum's role is to support them, not to judge or correct them.

heading: Planning and Tracking Are Separate, by Design
text: You can: Plan amounts for categories in advance Track transactions without planning anything Adjust plans during the month Overspend in one category and compensate in another The difference between the plan and what happened is useful information, not a failure. If you plan $500 and spend $600, the app shows the $100 difference; you don't need to change the plan afterwards to make it look right. Many people spend their first months mostly measuring: guess, track, and adjust the next month. Life doesn't reset on the first day of the month, so a new month can build on the last one. Copy Plan brings categories and planned amounts forward, and when a new month starts with no plan yet, the Budget screen offers to copy last month's plan.

heading: Real-Life Structure, Not Abstract Categories
text: You are not locked into a fixed category system. During setup you can pick from suggested categories or start from scratch. Sections group related areas of life (for example Housing, Food, Income) Categories are the specific things you plan and track, as broad or as specific as you like: "Kids" or "Diapers", "Groceries" or "Detergent" Sections and categories are one shared list used by every month, so renaming a category renames it everywhere and reports can follow it over time. Plans are separate for each month or custom period, so amounts can change as your life changes. You can also budget by calendar month or by your own periods, for example from payday to payday.

heading: Detail When You Need It, Simplicity When You Don't
text: Budgetum has grown a lot since its first version, but every extra is optional. You can keep things simple: Create a few categories Set a plan Add expenses See what happened Or you can go deeper: Split receipts into items Use accounts and transfers to see where your money is Use tags for trips, projects, or anything that crosses categories Track spending by store or person Analyze trends over time, on your phone or in Desktop Analytics on a computer Nothing is mandatory.

heading: No Bank Login
text: Budgetum never connects to your bank or asks for your bank login. You add transactions yourself, import a CSV file, or, with Pro, match a bank statement file (CSV or XLSX) against an account and approve its rows. Files are read on your device. This is a deliberate choice. A short regular review, for example once a week, keeps you looking at where your money goes instead of transactions arriving unseen in the background. It also means no other service needs access to your bank account.

heading: Calm, Pressure-Free Experience
text: Budgetum avoids tactics that create anxiety: No aggressive warnings No "you're doing it wrong" messages No ads No paywall in the core budgeting flow Planning, tracking, and analytics are free. Budgetum Pro is a one-time purchase, not a subscription. It unlocks advanced tools (more than 5 recurring transactions, more than 5 tags, Saved Sets, and bank statement matching) and supports development. A budgeting app shouldn't add another monthly bill. Say thanks in More → About is an optional tip for the developer. It doesn't unlock anything.

heading: Offline-First and Private
text: Budgetum works offline, and you don't need to create an account. Your budget is stored on your device. There is no Budgetum server holding your transactions. Backups are files you create and keep wherever you choose. A few optional extras use the internet: shared budget plan links (only when you create one), exchange-rate suggestions, and purchases. Desktop Analytics at budgetum.app/analytics opens an export in your computer's browser and reads it there, without uploading it. The app sends anonymous usage statistics and crash reports, which do not include your financial data. The Privacy Policy explains what is collected.

heading: A Tool, Not a Teacher
text: Budgetum does not try to educate you with financial ideology. Instead, it aims to: Show your data clearly Help you notice patterns Give you tools to organize money your way Better decisions come from understanding, not pressure.

heading: Budgetum in One Sentence
text: Budgetum is a flexible budgeting app that adapts to you, respects your choices, and helps you understand your money without stress. Understanding first. Rules second.
